+# ARS: Agentic Reward System for Robot Learning
+
+[![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2609.34484-b31b1b?style=flat-square)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34484)
+
+![ARS framework: event proposal, independent verification, and task progress estimation with adaptive visual inspection.](assets/framework.png)
+
+**ARS (Agentic Reward System)** estimates task progress from offline robot
+trajectories and task instructions using general-purpose vision-language models,
+without additional reward-model training. It combines adaptive visual inspection
+with cross-agent verification to track meaningful progress, failed attempts, and
+regressions.
+
+This repository contains the ARS implementation and code for constructing the
+semantic-mismatch benchmark.
+
+## Installation
+
+Use Python 3.11. From the repository root, run:
+
+```bash
+python3.11 -m venv .venv
+source .venv/bin/activate
+python -m pip install --upgrade pip
+python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+The default configuration uses **Qwen3.6-27B**. The tested inference setup uses
+**vLLM 0.19.1**, **PyTorch 2.10.0**, and **Transformers 5.9.0**,
+with the client and server in the same Python environment. Install vLLM in that
+environment using the shared dependency requirements:
+
+```bash
+python -m pip install -r requirements.txt "vllm==0.19.1"
+```
+
+See the [official deployment instructions](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B#vllm)
+for model-serving details.
+
+## Agent inference
+
+ARS takes a **LeRobot v2.1 dataset** containing trajectory images and task
+instructions. The current reader expects an `image` feature stored in the episode
+Parquet files. Pass a single dataset directory containing `meta/info.json`.
+
+Run the following commands from the repository root. Edit
+[configs/config.yaml](configs/config.yaml) for agent settings and
+[configs/server.yaml](configs/server.yaml) for the model path, GPU IDs, and vLLM
+options. Set `--allowed-local-media-path` to the absolute output directory or an
+ancestor directory, and keep server ports aligned with the endpoints in
+`configs/config.yaml`. The agent and server must share access to these paths.
+
+The default inference configuration was tested on GPUs with 96 GiB of VRAM each.
+
+Run the agent with automatic server startup:
+
+```bash
+python -m agent.cli run-batch \
+  --lerobot-root /path/to/lerobot_dataset \
+  --output-root /path/to/outputs \
+  --config configs/config.yaml \
+  --start-server configs/server.yaml
+```
+
+If you prefer to start vLLM manually, use the same model and vLLM arguments defined
+in `configs/server.yaml`. Set the server endpoints in `configs/config.yaml`, then
+run the agent without `--start-server`:
+
+```bash
+python -m agent.cli run-batch \
+  --lerobot-root /path/to/lerobot_dataset \
+  --output-root /path/to/outputs \
+  --config configs/config.yaml
+```
+
+Results are saved under `<output-root>/<batch-id>/`, where the batch ID is
+generated automatically. `batch_results.jsonl` records episode results and
+progress artifact paths.
+
+Optional terminal outcome labels and task references can be configured in
+[configs/config.yaml](configs/config.yaml#L30) and
+[configs/task_context.yaml](configs/task_context.yaml).
+
+### Audit external progress proposals
+
+ARS can audit external progress proposals against trajectory images and
+task instructions, correcting values unsupported by visual evidence.
+
+Provide a `batch_results.jsonl` manifest and its referenced per-episode
+progress CSVs, following the same format as ARS outputs. Each selected
+LeRobot episode must have exactly one completed result with a full
+frame-aligned progress curve normalized to `[0, 1]`.
+
+If your progress estimates come from another repository, please convert
+its outputs to this format before passing them to ARS.
+
+Add `--proposal-batch-results /path/to/batch_results.jsonl` to the `run-batch`
+command above. Audited results are saved under `<output-root>/<batch-id>/`
+in the standard ARS output format.
+
+## Multi-node inference with Ray
+
+ARS can distribute episodes across an existing Ray cluster. Install Ray in the
+agent environment using the cluster's version, and make the code, configuration,
+model weights, and dataset available at the same absolute paths on every node.
+The output directory must be shared across nodes.
+
+Add `--num-nodes` to the managed-server command:
+
+```bash
+python -m agent.cli run-batch \
+  --lerobot-root /path/to/lerobot_dataset \
+  --output-root /path/to/outputs \
+  --config configs/config.yaml \
+  --start-server configs/server.yaml \
+  --num-nodes 2
+```
+
+For multiple nodes, `--start-server` is required. Each node launches the server
+layout defined in `configs/server.yaml` and processes its assigned episodes.
+
+The batch directory contains `distributed_summary.json` and per-node result
+files under `nodes/`. Use all per-node `batch_results.jsonl` files for evaluation.
+
+## Semantic-mismatch benchmark
+
+### Collect trajectories
+
+We use an [adapted version](third_party)
+of [RL4VLA](https://github.com/gen-robot/RL4VLA)
+to collect trajectories and generate mismatched task instructions.
+This requires a **separate simulation environment**.
+The ARS inference environment does not include its simulation dependencies.
+
+Initialize the submodule:
+
+```bash
+git submodule update --init --recursive
+```
+
+Change into `third_party/RL4VLA`, then follow the installation instructions
+in its `README.md` to create its environment. Activate that environment before
+running the collection command from `third_party/RL4VLA/ManiSkill`:
+
+```bash
+python -m mani_skill.examples.motionplanning.widowx.collect_simpler \
+  -e "PutOnPlateInScene25MultiCarrot-v1" \
+  --save_video --save_data --num_procs 1 --num_traj 500 --seed=100 \
+  --obj-set all
+```
+
+Trajectory data from this command is saved under
+`third_party/RL4VLA/ManiSkill/mp_collect/PutOnPlateInScene25MultiCarrot-v1/500/data`.
+The collector includes incorrect task instructions and mismatch types for
+constructing the benchmark.
+
+### Convert to LeRobot v2.1
+
+After collection, return to the repository root and switch back to the ARS
+environment for LeRobot conversion, agent inference, and progress evaluation.
+
+```bash
+python scripts/convert_rl4vla_mp_collect_to_lerobot.py \
+  --input-root third_party/RL4VLA/ManiSkill/mp_collect/PutOnPlateInScene25MultiCarrot-v1/500/data \
+  --output-dir data/lerobot/semantic_mismatch \
+  --add-mismatch-failure
+```
+
+For the task above, the converter creates two samples from each successful
+trajectory: one with the correct instruction and one with an instruction
+referring to the other object in the scene. Both samples share the same images
+and actions. The correct-instruction sample is labeled as a success, and the
+mismatched-instruction sample is labeled as a failure.
+
+Use the resulting dataset as `--lerobot-root` when running ARS.
+
+### Progress evaluation
+
+Edit [scripts/evaluate_progress_score.yaml](scripts/evaluate_progress_score.yaml)
+to specify the dataset and completed `batch_results.jsonl` files. Paths are
+relative to the YAML file. Each episode must have exactly one completed result
+across the listed files.
+
+```bash
+python scripts/evaluate_progress_score.py \
+  --config scripts/evaluate_progress_score.yaml \
+  --output outputs/progress_scores.json
+```
+
+The benchmark reports:
+
+- **VOC:** correlation between estimated progress and time under correct
+  instructions.
+- **FPSR:** fraction of mismatch duration without positive progress increases.
+- **CMPG:** mean terminal progress under correct instructions minus mean peak
+  progress under mismatched instructions.
+
+## Citation
+
+If you find our work helpful, please cite the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34484):
+
+```bibtex
+@article{Hu2026ARS,
+  title         = {{ARS}: Agentic Reward System for Robot Learning},
+  author        = {Sheng Hu and Weiyi Lu and Lingbing Zeng and Gan Weng and
+                   Weiwei Zhang and Kai Xie and Xiaofeng Mou and Yi Xu},
+  journal       = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.34484},
+  year          = {2026},
+  eprint        = {2609.34484},
+  archivePrefix = {arXiv},
+  primaryClass  = {cs.RO},
+  url           = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34484}
+}
+```
+
+## License
+
+The ARS agent, scripts, and configuration are licensed under
+[Apache-2.0](LICENSE).
+
+Code under [`third_party/RL4VLA`](third_party) retains its respective
+upstream licenses. See the accompanying license files for details.

+"""Durable JSONL journal shared by reward and progress batch runners."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import tempfile
+import threading
+from dataclasses import asdict, is_dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Mapping
+
+import numpy as np
+
+
+class BatchJournal:
+    """Append durable batch events/results and atomically refresh a summary.
+
+    A journal represents one fresh process run.  It deliberately does not load
+    old terminal identities for skipping or merging; callers must apply their
+    overwrite/new-directory policy before constructing it.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, batch_dir: str | Path) -> None:
+        self.batch_dir = Path(batch_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+        self.batch_results = self.batch_dir / "batch_results.jsonl"
+        self.batch_events = self.batch_dir / "batch_events.jsonl"
+        self.batch_summary = self.batch_dir / "batch_summary.json"
+        self._lock = threading.RLock()
+        self._terminal_identities: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
+        self._results_existed_at_start = (
+            self.batch_results.is_file() and self.batch_results.stat().st_size > 0
+        )
+
+    def append_event(self, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+        """Durably append one event as exactly one strict UTF-8 JSON line."""
+
+        self._append_jsonl(self.batch_events, payload)
+
+    def append_terminal_result(self, row: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+        """Append one episode terminal row, rejecting same-run duplicates."""
+
+        identity = _terminal_identity(row)
+        with self._lock:
+            if self._results_existed_at_start:
+                raise FileExistsError(
+                    f"{self.batch_results} already contained terminal rows when "
+                    "this BatchJournal was created; resume/merge is not supported."
+                )
+            if identity in self._terminal_identities:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Duplicate terminal batch-result row in the current run for "
+                    f"{identity[0]}={identity[1]!r}."
+                )
+            # Record the identity only after the durable append succeeds.  A
+            # failed disk write may therefore be retried by the caller.
+            self._append_jsonl_unlocked(self.batch_results, row)
+            self._terminal_identities.add(identity)
+
+    def refresh_summary(self, base_payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+        """Atomically rewrite summary fields derived from durable terminal rows."""
+
+        with self._lock:
+            rows = self._read_terminal_results_unlocked()
+            status_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
+            for row in rows:
+                status = str(row.get("status", "unknown"))
+                status_counts[status] = status_counts.get(status, 0) + 1
+
+            payload = dict(base_payload)
+            payload["terminal_result_count"] = len(rows)
+            payload["status_counts"] = dict(sorted(status_counts.items()))
+            payload["completed_episodes"] = sum(
+                1 for row in rows if row.get("status") == "completed"
+            )
+            payload["failed_episodes"] = sum(
+                1 for row in rows if row.get("status") != "completed"
+            )
+            self._atomic_write_json_unlocked(self.batch_summary, payload)
+
+    def _append_jsonl(self, path: Path, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            self._append_jsonl_unlocked(path, payload)
+
+    def _append_jsonl_unlocked(
+        self,
+        path: Path,
+        payload: Mapping[str, Any],
+    ) -> None:
+        if not isinstance(payload, Mapping):
+            raise TypeError(f"JSONL payload must be a mapping, got {type(payload)!r}.")
+        encoded = json.dumps(
+            _json_ready(payload, batch_dir=self.batch_dir),
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        )
+        if "\n" in encoded or "\r" in encoded:
+            # json.dumps escapes control newlines inside strings, so a literal
+            # newline here would signal an unsafe/custom encoder regression.
+            raise ValueError("Serialized JSONL payload unexpectedly contains a newline.")
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
+            handle.write(encoded + "\n")
+            handle.flush()
+            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
+
+    def _read_terminal_results_unlocked(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+        if not self.batch_results.is_file():
+            return []
+        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+        with self.batch_results.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
+                stripped = raw_line.strip()
+                if not stripped:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    payload = json.loads(stripped)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        f"{self.batch_results}: invalid JSON on line {line_number}: {exc}"
+                    ) from exc
+                if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+                    raise TypeError(
+                        f"{self.batch_results}: line {line_number} must be a JSON object."
+                    )
+                rows.append(payload)
+        return rows
+
+    def _atomic_write_json_unlocked(
+        self,
+        path: Path,
+        payload: Mapping[str, Any],
+    ) -> None:
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        encoded = json.dumps(
+            _json_ready(payload, batch_dir=self.batch_dir),
+            indent=2,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+        ) + "\n"
+        descriptor, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
+            prefix=f".{path.name}.",
+            suffix=".tmp",
+            dir=path.parent,
+        )
+        temporary_path = Path(temporary_name)
+        try:
+            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
+                handle.write(encoded)
+                handle.flush()
+                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
+            os.replace(temporary_path, path)
+            # Persist the directory entry where the platform supports opening
+            # a directory descriptor.  The file itself was already fsynced.
+            try:
+                directory_fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
+            except OSError:
+                directory_fd = None
+            if directory_fd is not None:
+                try:
+                    os.fsync(directory_fd)
+                finally:
+                    os.close(directory_fd)
+        except Exception:
+            temporary_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+            raise
+
+

+        counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1

+def _batch_nonfatal_artifact_warnings(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    warnings: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

+        if not isinstance(row_warnings, list):

+        for warning in row_warnings:

+def _write_json(path: Path, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:

+    return digest.hexdigest()

+def _json_ready(value: Any) -> Any:
+    if isinstance(value, Path):
+        return str(value)
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return {str(key): _json_ready(item) for key, item in value.items()}
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return [_json_ready(item) for item in value]
+    if isinstance(value, tuple):
+        return [_json_ready(item) for item in value]
+    return value

+    if external_endpoints:

+        )

+        lerobot_root=args.lerobot_root,
+        output_root=args.output_root,

+        server_config=args.start_server,
+        num_nodes=num_nodes,

+def _resolve_batch_endpoints_from_args(
+    args: argparse.Namespace,
+    config: RewardAgentConfig,

+    list[ResolvedEndpoint],
+    list[ResolvedEndpoint],

+]:
+    server_endpoints: list[ResolvedEndpoint] = []
+    startup_config: ServerStartupConfig | None = None
+    if args.start_server is not None:
+        server_payload = load_server_config(args.start_server)
+        startup_config = resolve_server_startup_config(server_payload.get("startup"))
+        server_endpoints = resolve_server_groups(server_payload.get("server_groups", []))
+
+    endpoints = [
+        endpoint.strip()
+        for endpoint in str(args.endpoints or "").split(",")
+        if endpoint.strip()
+    ]
+    if endpoints:
+        client_endpoints = resolve_client_endpoint_groups(
+            [

+                    "name": "cli_external",
+                    "max_concurrent": int(args.max_concurrent_per_endpoint),
+                    "endpoints": endpoints,
+                }
+            ]
+        )
+    elif config.vllm.endpoint_groups:
+        client_endpoints = resolve_client_endpoint_groups(list(config.vllm.endpoint_groups))
+    elif server_endpoints:
+        client_endpoints = derive_client_endpoints_from_server(

+        raise ValueError(
+            "run-batch requires vllm.endpoint_groups in --config, --endpoints, "
+            "or --start-server so client endpoints can be derived."
+        )

+    if server_endpoints:

+            client_endpoints=client_endpoints,
+            server_endpoints=server_endpoints,
+        )

+def _load_config_from_args(args: argparse.Namespace) -> RewardAgentConfig:
+    overrides: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    if getattr(args, "base_url", None) is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("vllm", {})["base_url"] = args.base_url
+    if args.model is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("vllm", {})["model"] = args.model
+    if args.context_window is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("vllm", {})["context_window"] = args.context_window
+    if args.timeout_seconds is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("vllm", {})["timeout_seconds"] = args.timeout_seconds
+    if args.media_mode is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("visual", {})["media_mode"] = args.media_mode
+    if args.max_attached_frames_per_call is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("visual", {})["max_attached_frames_per_call"] = args.max_attached_frames_per_call
+    if getattr(args, "max_retries", None) is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("batch", {})["max_retries"] = args.max_retries
+    if getattr(args, "episode_indices", None) is not None:
+        overrides.setdefault("batch", {})["episode_indices"] = args.episode_indices
+
+    if args.config is not None:
+        return RewardAgentConfig.from_yaml(args.config, overrides=overrides)
+    if overrides:
+        return RewardAgentConfig.from_dict(overrides)
+    return RewardAgentConfig.default()
+
+
+def _parse_episode_indices_arg(raw_value: str) -> list[int]:
+    """Parse a shell-friendly comma-separated episode_index list."""
+
+    text = str(raw_value).strip()
+    if not text:
+        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("--episode-indices must be a non-empty comma-separated list.")
+
+    indices: list[int] = []
+    seen: set[int] = set()
+    for position, token in enumerate(text.split(",")):
+        stripped = token.strip()
+        if not stripped:
+            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+                f"--episode-indices contains an empty item at position {position}."
+            )
+        try:
+            value = int(stripped)
+        except ValueError as exc:
+            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+                f"--episode-indices item {stripped!r} is not an integer."
+            ) from exc
+        if value < 0:
+            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+                f"--episode-indices item {stripped!r} must be non-negative."
+            )
+        if value in seen:
+            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+                f"--episode-indices contains duplicate episode_index {value}."
+            )
+        seen.add(value)
+        indices.append(value)
+    return indices
+
+
+def _parse_positive_int_arg(raw_value: str) -> int:
+    """Parse a strictly positive CLI integer without accepting floats."""
+
+    try:
+        value = int(raw_value)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+            f"expected a positive integer, got {raw_value!r}."
+        ) from exc
+    if value <= 0:
+        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+            f"expected a positive integer, got {raw_value!r}."
+        )
+    return value
+
+
+def _parse_positive_float_arg(raw_value: str) -> float:
+    """Parse a finite positive CLI duration."""
+
+    try:
+        value = float(raw_value)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+            f"expected a positive number, got {raw_value!r}."
+        ) from exc
+    if not (value > 0.0) or value == float("inf"):
+        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
+            f"expected a finite positive number, got {raw_value!r}."
+        )
+    return value
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Small OpenAI-compatible HTTP client for the externally managed vLLM server."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.request
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+from .config import GenerationConfig, VllmConfig
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ChatResponse:
+    """Parsed subset of a chat completion response."""
+
+    message: dict[str, Any]
+    usage: dict[str, Any]
+    raw: dict[str, Any]
+
+
+class VllmChatClient:
+    """HTTP client for vLLM's OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+        generation_config: GenerationConfig,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self.generation_config = generation_config
+
+    def readiness_check(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Verify that the server is reachable and exposes the expected model."""
+
+        models = self._request_json("GET", self.vllm_config.models_url)
+        model_ids = [str(item.get("id")) for item in models.get("data", []) if isinstance(item, dict)]
+        if model_ids and self.vllm_config.model not in model_ids:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"vLLM server is reachable, but model {self.vllm_config.model!r} "
+                f"is not listed. Available models: {model_ids}"
+            )
+        return {"ok": True, "models": model_ids}
+
+    def reset_server_cache(self, *, include_mm_cache: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Call dev-mode cache reset endpoints when explicitly requested."""
+
+        results: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        results["reset_prefix_cache"] = self._request_json(
+            "POST",
+            f"{self.vllm_config.root_url}/reset_prefix_cache",
+        )
+        if include_mm_cache:
+            results["reset_mm_cache"] = self._request_json(
+                "POST",
+                f"{self.vllm_config.root_url}/reset_mm_cache",
+            )
+        return results
+
+    def chat(
+        self,
+        *,
+        messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
+        tools: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
+        final_step: bool = False,
+        generation_overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> ChatResponse:
+        """Send one chat completion request."""
+
+        payload = {
+            "model": self.vllm_config.model,
+            "messages": messages,
+            **self.generation_config.to_request_payload(
+                final_step=final_step,
+                overrides=generation_overrides,
+            ),
+        }
+        if tools:
+            payload["tools"] = tools
+            payload["tool_choice"] = "auto"
+        raw = self._request_json("POST", self.vllm_config.chat_url, payload=payload)
+        choices = raw.get("choices") or []
+        if not choices:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Chat completion response has no choices: {raw}")
+        message = choices[0].get("message")
+        if not isinstance(message, dict):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Chat completion choice has no message object: {choices[0]}")
+        usage = raw.get("usage") or {}
+        return ChatResponse(message=message, usage=usage if isinstance(usage, dict) else {}, raw=raw)
+
+    def _request_json(
+        self,
+        method: str,
+        url: str,
+        *,
+        payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        data = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
+        request = urllib.request.Request(
+            url,
+            data=data,
+            method=method,
+            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
+        )
+        try:
+            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=self.vllm_config.timeout_seconds) as response:
+                text = response.read().decode("utf-8")
+        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
+            body = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+            raise RuntimeError(f"vLLM HTTP {exc.code} for {url}: {body}") from exc
+        except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Could not reach vLLM server at {url}: {exc}") from exc
+        if not text.strip():
+            return {}
+        payload = json.loads(text)
+        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Expected JSON object from {url}, got {type(payload).__name__}.")
+        return payload

+def _require_boolean(value: Any, *, field_name: str) -> bool:
+    """Require a native YAML/JSON boolean without truthiness coercion."""
+
+    if type(value) is not bool:
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"{field_name} must be a boolean, got {type(value).__name__}."
+        )
+    return value

+def _validate_boolean_mapping_keys(
+    payload: dict[str, Any],
+    *,
+    field_prefix: str,
+    keys: tuple[str, ...],
+) -> None:
+    """Validate known boolean keys while leaving unrelated extension keys untouched."""
+
+    for key in keys:
+        if key in payload:
+            _require_boolean(payload[key], field_name=f"{field_prefix}.{key}")

+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class GenerationConfig:
+    """Model sampling settings used for every chat call unless a stage overrides them."""
+
+    temperature: float = 0.0
+    top_p: float = 1.0
+    top_k: int = 0
+    min_p: float = 0.0
+    presence_penalty: float = 0.0
+    frequency_penalty: float = 0.0
+    repetition_penalty: float = 1.0
+    seed: int = 0
+    max_tokens_per_step: int = 8192
+    max_tokens_final: int = 8192
+    reserved_output_tokens: int = 2048
+    thinking_token_budget: int | None = None
+    thinking_budget_forced_end_phrase: str | None = None
+    chat_template_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=lambda: {"enable_thinking": True})
+
+    def to_request_payload(
+        self,
+        *,
+        final_step: bool = False,
+        overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        values = {
+            key: getattr(self, key)
+            for key in self.__dataclass_fields__
+        }
+        stage_overrides = dict(overrides or {})
+        for key, value in stage_overrides.items():
+            if key == "chat_template_kwargs" and isinstance(value, dict):
+                merged_kwargs = dict(values["chat_template_kwargs"])
+                merged_kwargs.update(value)
+                values[key] = merged_kwargs
+            elif key in values:
+                values[key] = value
+
+        payload = {
+            "temperature": float(values["temperature"]),
+            "top_p": float(values["top_p"]),
+            "top_k": int(values["top_k"]),
+            "min_p": float(values["min_p"]),
+            "presence_penalty": float(values["presence_penalty"]),
+            "frequency_penalty": float(values["frequency_penalty"]),
+            "repetition_penalty": float(values["repetition_penalty"]),
+            "seed": int(values["seed"]),
+            "max_tokens": int(values["max_tokens_final"] if final_step else values["max_tokens_per_step"]),
+            "chat_template_kwargs": dict(values["chat_template_kwargs"]),
+        }
+        # vLLM treats thinking_token_budget as a request-level sampling
+        # parameter. Keep it absent unless explicitly configured so servers
+        # without --reasoning-config continue to work.
+        if values["thinking_token_budget"] is not None:
+            payload["thinking_token_budget"] = int(values["thinking_token_budget"])
+        return payload

+        if not common_prompt:

+        stages = tuple(StageSpec.from_dict(stage) for stage in data.get("stages", ()))
+        if not stages:
+            raise ValueError("Workflow must contain at least one stage.")
+        return cls(
+            name=name,
+            common_prompt=common_prompt,
+            stages=stages,
+            source_path=source_path,
+        )
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class RewardAgentConfig:
+    """Top-level harness configuration."""
+
+    vllm: VllmConfig = field(default_factory=VllmConfig)
+    generation: GenerationConfig = field(default_factory=GenerationConfig)
+    progress: ProgressConfig = field(default_factory=ProgressConfig)
+    visual: VisualConfig = field(default_factory=VisualConfig)
+    task_context: TaskContextConfig = field(default_factory=TaskContextConfig)
+    is_success_ground_truth: IsSuccessGroundTruthConfig = field(
+        default_factory=IsSuccessGroundTruthConfig
+    )
+    batch: BatchConfig = field(default_factory=BatchConfig)
+    workflow: WorkflowSpec | None = None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def default(cls) -> "RewardAgentConfig":
+        workflow = load_workflow(DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_RESOURCE)
+        return cls(workflow=workflow)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_yaml(
+        cls,
+        path: str | Path,
+        *,
+        overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> "RewardAgentConfig":
+        with Path(path).expanduser().open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            payload = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}
+        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+            raise ValueError(f"Config YAML must contain a mapping, got {type(payload).__name__}.")
+        if overrides:
+            payload = _deep_merge_dicts(payload, overrides)
+        return cls.from_dict(payload)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_dict(cls, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> "RewardAgentConfig":
+        workflow_value = payload.get("workflow")
+        if isinstance(workflow_value, WorkflowSpec):
+            workflow = workflow_value
+        elif isinstance(workflow_value, str):
+            workflow = load_workflow(workflow_value)
+        elif isinstance(workflow_value, dict):
+            workflow_path = workflow_value.get("path")
+            workflow = load_workflow(str(workflow_path)) if workflow_path else WorkflowSpec.from_dict(
+                workflow_value,
+                source_path="<inline>",
+            )
+        else:
+            workflow = load_workflow(DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_RESOURCE)
+
+        vllm_payload = dict(payload.get("vllm", {}) or {})
+        if "endpoint_groups" in vllm_payload:
+            vllm_payload["endpoint_groups"] = tuple(
+                dict(group) for group in (vllm_payload.get("endpoint_groups") or ())
+            )
+        generation_payload = payload.get("generation", {}) or {}
+        progress_payload = payload.get("progress", {}) or {}
+        visual_payload = payload.get("visual", {}) or {}
+        task_context_payload = payload.get("task_context", {}) or {}
+        is_success_ground_truth_payload = (
+            payload["is_success_ground_truth"]
+            if "is_success_ground_truth" in payload
+            else {}
+        )
+        batch_payload = payload["batch"] if "batch" in payload else {}
+        if not isinstance(task_context_payload, dict):
+            raise TypeError("task_context must be a mapping with path/require_all_matched fields.")
+        if not isinstance(is_success_ground_truth_payload, dict):
+            raise TypeError("is_success_ground_truth must be a mapping with an enabled field.")
+        if not isinstance(batch_payload, dict):
+            raise TypeError("batch must be a mapping with max_retries/episode_indices fields.")
+        return cls(
+            vllm=VllmConfig(**_filter_dataclass_kwargs(VllmConfig, vllm_payload)),
+            generation=GenerationConfig(**_filter_dataclass_kwargs(GenerationConfig, generation_payload)),
+            progress=ProgressConfig(**_filter_dataclass_kwargs(ProgressConfig, progress_payload)),
+            visual=_load_visual_config(visual_payload),
+            task_context=TaskContextConfig(
+                **_filter_dataclass_kwargs(TaskContextConfig, task_context_payload)
+            ),
+            is_success_ground_truth=IsSuccessGroundTruthConfig(
+                **_filter_dataclass_kwargs(
+                    IsSuccessGroundTruthConfig,
+                    is_success_ground_truth_payload,
+                )
+            ),
+            batch=BatchConfig(**_filter_dataclass_kwargs(BatchConfig, batch_payload)),
+            workflow=workflow,
+        )
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        data = asdict(self)
+        if self.workflow is not None:
+            data["workflow"] = asdict(self.workflow)
+        return data
+
+
+def load_workflow(path: str | Path) -> WorkflowSpec:
+    """Load a workflow from a package resource or a filesystem path."""
+
+    text, source_path = _read_resource_or_file(path)
+    payload = yaml.safe_load(text) or {}
+    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"Workflow YAML must contain a mapping, got {type(payload).__name__}.")
+    workflow = WorkflowSpec.from_dict(payload, source_path=source_path)
+    prompt_paths = [workflow.common_prompt] + [stage.prompt for stage in workflow.stages]
+    prompt_hashes = {
+        prompt_path: _short_hash(load_prompt_text(prompt_path))
+        for prompt_path in prompt_paths
+    }
+    return WorkflowSpec(
+        name=workflow.name,
+        common_prompt=workflow.common_prompt,
+        stages=workflow.stages,
+        source_path=workflow.source_path,
+        prompt_hashes=prompt_hashes,
+    )
+
+
+def load_prompt_text(path: str | Path) -> str:
+    """Load prompt text from the reward-agent package or a direct file path."""
+
+    text, _source_path = _read_resource_or_file(path)
+    return text.rstrip() + "\n"
+
+
+def _read_resource_or_file(path: str | Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    raw_path = Path(path).expanduser()
+    if raw_path.is_file():
+        return raw_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), str(raw_path.resolve())
+
+    resource_path = str(path).strip().replace("\\", "/")
+    if resource_path.startswith("agent/"):
+        resource_path = resource_path.removeprefix("agent/")
+    package_root = files("agent")
+    resource = package_root.joinpath(resource_path)
+    if not resource.is_file():
+        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Reward-agent resource not found: {path}")
+    return resource.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), f"agent/{resource_path}"
+
+
+def _filter_dataclass_kwargs(cls: type[Any], payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    allowed = set(getattr(cls, "__dataclass_fields__", {}))
+    return {key: value for key, value in dict(payload).items() if key in allowed}
+
+
+def _normalize_episode_indices(raw_value: Any, *, field_name: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Validate an optional explicit LeRobot episode_index schedule."""
+
+    if raw_value is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(raw_value, str) or not isinstance(raw_value, (list, tuple)):
+        raise TypeError(f"{field_name} must be null or a non-empty list of non-negative integers.")
+    if not raw_value:
+        raise ValueError(f"{field_name} must be null or a non-empty list of non-negative integers.")
+
+    indices: list[int] = []
+    seen: set[int] = set()
+    for position, value in enumerate(raw_value):
+        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
+            raise TypeError(f"{field_name}[{position}] must be a non-negative integer.")
+        if value < 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"{field_name}[{position}] must be a non-negative integer.")
+        if value in seen:
+            raise ValueError(f"{field_name} contains duplicate episode_index {value}.")
+        seen.add(value)
+        indices.append(value)
+    return tuple(indices)
+
+
+def _load_visual_config(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> VisualConfig:
+    """Build VisualConfig while preserving nested external_label_bar structure."""
+
+    visual_kwargs = _filter_dataclass_kwargs(VisualConfig, payload)
+    label_payload = visual_kwargs.pop("external_label_bar", {}) or {}
+    if not isinstance(label_payload, dict):
+        raise TypeError("visual.external_label_bar must be a mapping with enabled/video/tile fields.")
+    visual_kwargs["external_label_bar"] = _load_external_label_bar_config(label_payload)
+    return VisualConfig(**visual_kwargs)
+
+
+def _load_external_label_bar_config(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> ExternalLabelBarConfig:
+    """Build nested label-bar config from YAML dictionaries."""
+
+    video_payload = payload.get("video", {}) or {}
+    tile_payload = payload.get("tile", {}) or {}
+    if not isinstance(video_payload, dict):
+        raise TypeError("visual.external_label_bar.video must be a mapping.")
+    if not isinstance(tile_payload, dict):
+        raise TypeError("visual.external_label_bar.tile must be a mapping.")
+    _validate_boolean_mapping_keys(
+        video_payload,
+        field_prefix="visual.external_label_bar.video",
+        keys=("frame", "progress"),
+    )
+    _validate_boolean_mapping_keys(
+        tile_payload,
+        field_prefix="visual.external_label_bar.tile",
+        keys=("frame", "progress"),
+    )
+    return ExternalLabelBarConfig(
+        enabled=payload.get("enabled", False),
+        video=LabelBarModeConfig(**_filter_dataclass_kwargs(LabelBarModeConfig, video_payload)),
+        tile=LabelBarModeConfig(**_filter_dataclass_kwargs(LabelBarModeConfig, tile_payload)),
+    )
+
+
+def _validate_stage_tool_config(*, stage_id: str, tool_config: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Validate stage-local tool policy values that affect tool schemas."""
+
+    if not isinstance(tool_config, dict):
+        raise TypeError(f"Workflow stage {stage_id!r} tool_config must be a mapping.")
+    inspect_config = tool_config.get("inspect_visual")
+    if inspect_config is None:
+        return
+    if not isinstance(inspect_config, dict):
+        raise TypeError(f"Workflow stage {stage_id!r} tool_config.inspect_visual must be a mapping.")
+
+    mode = str(inspect_config.get("mode", "model")).strip()
+    if mode not in {"model", "video", "tile"}:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Workflow stage {stage_id!r} tool_config.inspect_visual.mode must be "
+            f"'model', 'video', or 'tile', got {mode!r}."
+        )
+
+    sample_every_n = inspect_config.get("sample_every_n", "model")
+    if str(sample_every_n).strip() != "model":
+        if isinstance(sample_every_n, bool):
+            raise TypeError(
+                f"Workflow stage {stage_id!r} tool_config.inspect_visual.sample_every_n "
+                "must be 'model' or a positive integer."
+            )
+        try:
+            parsed_sample_every_n = int(sample_every_n)
+        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+            raise TypeError(
+                f"Workflow stage {stage_id!r} tool_config.inspect_visual.sample_every_n "
+                "must be 'model' or a positive integer."
+            ) from exc
+        if parsed_sample_every_n <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Workflow stage {stage_id!r} tool_config.inspect_visual.sample_every_n "
+                "must be a positive integer when fixed."
+            )
+
+    crop = str(inspect_config.get("crop", "enabled")).strip()
+    if crop not in {"enabled", "disabled"}:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Workflow stage {stage_id!r} tool_config.inspect_visual.crop must be "
+            f"'enabled' or 'disabled', got {crop!r}."
+        )
+
+
+def _deep_merge_dicts(base: dict[str, Any], override: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    merged = dict(base)
+    for key, value in override.items():
+        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(merged.get(key), dict):
+            merged[key] = _deep_merge_dicts(merged[key], value)
+        else:
+            merged[key] = value
+    return merged
+
+
+def _short_hash(text: str) -> str:
+    import hashlib
+
+    return hashlib.sha1(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]

+"""Terminal diagnostics for reward-agent runs."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import sys
+from typing import Any
+
+
+def emit_terminal_warning(message: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Print model-protocol warnings that should be visible during runs."""
+
+    print(f"[reward-agent warning] {message}: {terminal_payload(payload)}", file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+def emit_terminal_error(message: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Print harness/tool errors that need immediate terminal visibility."""
+
+    print(f"[reward-agent error] {message}: {terminal_payload(payload)}", file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+def emit_terminal_blocker(message: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Print deterministic gate blockers separately from Python exceptions."""
+
+    print(f"[reward-agent blocker] {message}: {terminal_payload(payload)}", file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+def tool_blocker_payload(
+    *,
+    stage_id: str,
+    tool_call_id: str,
+    name: str,
+    result: dict[str, Any],
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return a compact payload for tool results that explicitly report ok=false."""
+
+    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "stage_id": stage_id,
+        "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
+        "name": name,
+        "ok": bool(result.get("ok")),
+        "status": str(result.get("status") or "unknown"),
+    }
+    for key in ("blocked_items", "next_required_actions", "warnings"):
+        if key in result:
+            payload[key] = result[key]
+
+    data = result.get("data")
+    if not isinstance(data, dict):
+        return payload
+
+    for key in (
+        "invalid_observation_ids",
+        "progress",
+        "confirmed_observation_coverage",
+    ):
+        if key in data:
+            payload[key] = data[key]
+
+    validation = data.get("validation")
+    if isinstance(validation, dict):
+        payload["validation"] = {
+            key: validation[key]
+            for key in ("ok", "status", "blocked_items", "warnings")
+            if key in validation
+        }
+    return payload
+
+
+def terminal_payload(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    """Return a compact one-line payload for terminal diagnostics."""
+
+    display = dict(payload)
+    if "content" in display:
+        display["content"] = summarize_text(display["content"])
+    if "raw_arguments" in display:
+        display["raw_arguments"] = summarize_raw_arguments(display["raw_arguments"])
+    return json.dumps(display, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
+
+
+def summarize_raw_arguments(value: Any, *, limit: int = 500) -> Any:
+    """Keep invalid or oversized tool arguments readable in stderr output."""
+
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return summarize_text(value, limit=limit)
+    return value
+
+
+def summarize_text(value: Any, *, limit: int = 500) -> str | None:
+    """Return a single-line preview of model text for terminal diagnostics."""
+
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    text = str(value).replace("\n", "\\n")
+    if len(text) <= limit:
+        return text
+    return f"{text[:limit]}...<truncated {len(text) - limit} chars>"

+"""Episode-source boundary for reward-agent inputs."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Protocol, Sequence
+
+import imageio.v2 as imageio
+import numpy as np
+
+from .progress import load_progress_csv
+from .is_success import read_metadata_is_success
+from .schemas import ProgressRow
+from .visual import read_selected_frames
+
+
+class RewardAgentEpisodeSource(Protocol):
+    """Small interface that lets sessions avoid depending on one storage format."""
+
+    case_id: str
+    source_traj_id: str
+    episode_index: int
+    num_frames: int
+    source_fps: float | None
+    source_root: Path
+    video_path: Path | None
+
+    def read_task(self) -> str:
+        """Return the natural-language robot instruction."""
+
+    def read_metadata(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Return public episode metadata used by reward-agent tools."""
+
+    def read_progress_rows(self) -> list[ProgressRow] | None:
+        """Return optional candidate progress rows in the source frame axis."""
+
+    def read_is_success(self) -> bool:
+        """Return the required terminal success ground truth."""
+
+    def read_selected_frames(self, frame_indices: Sequence[int]) -> list[np.ndarray]:
+        """Return RGB frames for the requested source frame indices."""
+
+
+class CasePackEpisodeSource:
+    """Adapter for the existing sanitized case-pack directory format."""
+
+    def __init__(self, case_dir: str | Path, *, value_max_points: int) -> None:
+        self.source_root = Path(case_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+        if not self.source_root.is_dir():
+            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Case directory not found: {self.source_root}")
+        self.case_id = self.source_root.name
+        self.source_traj_id = self.case_id
+        self.episode_index = int(self.read_metadata().get("episode_index", -1))
+        self._value_max_points = int(value_max_points)
+        self.source_fps = _positive_float_or_none(self.read_metadata().get("fps"))
+        self.video_path = self._resolve_video_path()
+        self.num_frames = self._resolve_num_frames()
+
+    def read_task(self) -> str:
+        path = self.source_root / "task.txt"
+        if not path.is_file():
+            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Required case file not found: {path}")
+        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
+
+    def read_metadata(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        path = self.source_root / "metadata.json"
+        if not path.is_file():
+            return {}
+        payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+            raise ValueError(f"{path} must contain a JSON object.")
+        return payload
+
+    def read_progress_rows(self) -> list[ProgressRow] | None:
+        progress_path = self.source_root / "progress.csv"
+        if not progress_path.is_file():
+            return None
+        return load_progress_csv(
+            progress_path,
+            value_max_points=self._value_max_points,
+        )
+
+    def read_is_success(self) -> bool:
+        """Read the required terminal success label from metadata.json."""
+
+        metadata_path = self.source_root / "metadata.json"
+        if not metadata_path.is_file():
+            raise FileNotFoundError(
+                f"{metadata_path}: is_success_ground_truth.enabled=true requires metadata.json."
+            )
+        return read_metadata_is_success(
+            self.read_metadata(),
+            metadata_path=metadata_path,
+        )
+
+    def read_selected_frames(self, frame_indices: Sequence[int]) -> list[np.ndarray]:
+        if self.video_path is None:
+            raise FileNotFoundError(f"No video file could be resolved under {self.source_root}.")
+        return read_selected_frames(self.video_path, frame_indices)
+
+    def _resolve_video_path(self) -> Path | None:
+        metadata = self.read_metadata()
+        metadata_video = metadata.get("video_path") or metadata.get("video_file")
+        candidates: list[Path] = []
+        if metadata_video:
+            candidate = Path(str(metadata_video)).expanduser()
+            candidates.append(candidate if candidate.is_absolute() else self.source_root / candidate)
+        candidates.extend(
+            [
+                self.source_root / "video.mp4",
+                self.source_root / "trajectory.mp4",
+            ]
+        )
+        for candidate in candidates:
+            resolved = candidate.resolve()
+            if resolved.is_file():
+                return resolved
+        return None
+
+    def _resolve_num_frames(self) -> int:
+        metadata = self.read_metadata()
+        metadata_frames = metadata.get("num_frames")
+        if metadata_frames is not None:
+            count = int(metadata_frames)
+            if count <= 0:
+                raise ValueError(f"metadata.num_frames must be positive, got {count}.")
+            return count
+        if self.video_path is None:
+            raise ValueError("Cannot infer frame count without metadata.num_frames or a video file.")
+        reader = imageio.get_reader(self.video_path)
+        try:
+            count = int(reader.count_frames())
+        finally:
+            reader.close()
+        if count <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Video has no decodable frames: {self.video_path}")
+        return count
+
+
+def _positive_float_or_none(value: Any) -> float | None:
+    """Return a positive float metadata value when one is present."""
+
+    if value is None or isinstance(value, bool):
+        return None
+    try:
+        parsed = float(value)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return None
+    return parsed if parsed > 0 else None

+"""Strict readers for terminal ``is_success`` ground-truth labels."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Mapping
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+def read_metadata_is_success(metadata: Mapping[str, Any], *, metadata_path: Path) -> bool:
+    """Read one required JSON boolean from a case-pack metadata object."""
+
+    if "is_success" not in metadata:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{metadata_path}: is_success_ground_truth.enabled=true requires "
+            "a boolean 'is_success' field."
+        )
+    value = metadata["is_success"]
+    if not isinstance(value, bool):
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"{metadata_path}: 'is_success' must be a JSON boolean, "
+            f"got {type(value).__name__}."
+        )
+    return value
+
+
+def read_lerobot_is_success(episode_path: Path, *, expected_length: int) -> bool:
+    """Read and validate one constant boolean label from a LeRobot episode."""
+
+    path = Path(episode_path).expanduser().resolve()
+    try:
+        # This metadata read runs frequently in short-lived evaluator subprocesses.
+        # PyArrow's threaded Parquet path can intermittently abort while those
+        # processes are shutting down, so read the single label column serially.
+        frame = pd.read_parquet(
+            path,
+            columns=["is_success"],
+            use_threads=False,
+        )
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - normalize parquet/schema failures with episode context.
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{path}: is_success_ground_truth.enabled=true requires a readable "
+            "'is_success' column."
+        ) from exc
+
+    if len(frame) != int(expected_length):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{path}: expected {expected_length} is_success rows, got {len(frame)}."
+        )
+    if len(frame) == 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: episode has no is_success rows.")
+
+    values = [
+        _strict_boolean_scalar(value, label=f"{path}.is_success[{index}]")
+        for index, value in enumerate(frame["is_success"].tolist())
+    ]
+    unique_values = set(values)
+    if len(unique_values) != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: is_success must be constant within an episode.")
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _strict_boolean_scalar(value: Any, *, label: str) -> bool:
+    """Accept scalar-shaped bool values without coercing numbers or strings."""
+
+    array = np.asarray(value)
+    if array.size != 1:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{label} must contain exactly one boolean scalar, got shape {array.shape}."
+        )
+    scalar = array.reshape(-1)[0]
+    if not isinstance(scalar, (bool, np.bool_)):
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"{label} must be a boolean scalar, got {type(scalar).__name__}."
+        )
+    return bool(scalar)

+def build_progress_sample_indices(*, num_frames: int, max_frames: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Uniformly sample progress frames while keeping both episode endpoints.

+    same index construction.  Keeping the helper next to the canonical progress
+    contract prevents those two paths from drifting over time.
+    """

+    if num_frames <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"num_frames must be positive, got {num_frames}.")
+    if num_frames == 1:
+        return np.array([0], dtype=np.int64)
+    if max_frames < 2:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "max_frames must be at least 2 for multi-frame episodes so both "
+            f"the first and final frames can be sampled, got {max_frames}."
+        )
+
+    num_sampled = min(int(num_frames), int(max_frames))
+    if num_sampled == num_frames:
+        return np.arange(num_frames, dtype=np.int64)
+
+    rounded = np.rint(np.linspace(0, num_frames - 1, num_sampled)).astype(np.int64)
+    rounded[0] = 0
+    rounded[-1] = num_frames - 1

+    # The floor-linspace fallback keeps the axis increasing and pins both ends.
+    if len(set(int(index) for index in rounded.tolist())) != num_sampled:
+        rounded = np.linspace(0, num_frames - 1, num_sampled, dtype=np.int64)
+        rounded[0] = 0
+        rounded[-1] = num_frames - 1
+
+    if np.any(np.diff(rounded) <= 0):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Internal sampling error: expected increasing indices, got {rounded.tolist()}."
+        )
+    return rounded

+
+Inspect attached media directly before making visual claims. Treat `asset_id`,
+`frame_range`, and `frame_indices` as bookkeeping that identifies evidence, not
+as visual evidence by itself.
+
+Do not claim to have inspected frames or video segments that were not attached
+by the runner or returned by a visual evidence tool.
+
+## Frame Indexing
+
+Use attached videos from the trajectory being evaluated as frame-indexed
+videos, not real-time videos.
+
+Do not report time in minutes, seconds, or `mm:ss` format. Treat every timestamp
+value as an indexing unit, not real time. When `metadata.agent_video_fps` is
+`1`, visible timestamps label temporal groups of original frames rather than
+individual frames. A normal two-frame group containing frames `N` and `N + 1`
+is labeled `<N + 0.5 seconds>` and should be interpreted as frame group
+`[N, N + 1]`, not only frame `N`. For example, `<68.5 seconds>` corresponds
+to frame group `[68, 69]`, not only frame `68`. If the final temporal group
+contains one unpaired final frame `L`, its timestamp is `<L.0 seconds>` and
+should be interpreted as frame `L` alone. A terminal `<14.0 seconds>` in a
+15-frame attachment means frame `14` alone, not frames `[14, 15]`.
+
+All tool frame ranges use original 0-based frame indices and are closed
+intervals: both `start_frame` and `end_frame` are included. Choose the best
+visible integer frame boundaries. If an exact transition frame is visually
+unclear after focused inspection, still choose the best supported integer frame
+boundary and reflect uncertainty through confidence and the observation or edit
+reason.
+
+Do not choose event boundaries because they are numerically convenient, round,
+tidy, evenly spaced, or inherited from a coarse proposal. This includes common
+grid-like frame values such as values ending in 0 or 5, unless the visual
+transition itself is best supported there. Non-round and irregular frame numbers
+are expected when they better match the visible event.
+
+## Terminal Truncation
+
+Some trajectories may come from simulators that stop immediately once the task
+success condition is reached. Absence of post-success dwell, settling, or
+stabilization frames at the very end of the video is not by itself evidence of
+failure, partial success, or instability.
+
+Do not infer success merely because a video ends. Judge the terminal frames by
+the visible task-relevant state. If the required final condition is already
+visibly satisfied at the last available frames, treat the trajectory as
+completed even if no later stabilization interval is shown. If the final state
+is visibly slipping, falling, moving away, misaligned, dropped, or otherwise
+breaking the task condition before the video ends, treat that as instability.
+
+## Tool Discipline
+
+Use tools as the deterministic interface to the case. State-mutating tools
+should be called deliberately and sequentially so the trace stays auditable.
+
+Every tool result is a JSON envelope with top-level `ok`, `status`, `data`, and
+`warnings` fields. For successful calls, read the tool-specific payload from
+`data`, not from the top level. If `status="blocked"`, follow the top-level
+`blocked_items` and `next_required_actions` before retrying. If
+`status="error"`, fix the tool arguments or tool choice using the top-level
+`error.type` and `error.message`.
+
+After visual media is attached, normally call the next relevant tool rather
+than writing a long prose analysis. Put concise visual statements inside tool
+arguments such as observation text in observation-writing stages or progress
+edit reasons in the progress stage.
+
+Do not rely on a `status="error"` tool request as inspected evidence.
+
+## Visual Inspection Tool
+
+When `inspect_visual` is available, use it to request bounded visual evidence
+from the hidden raw video. Always include the original 0-based closed frame
+interval and a concrete `reason`.
+
+The exact argument schema for `inspect_visual` can change by stage. Use exactly
+the arguments exposed in the current stage's tool schema. If `mode`,
+`sample_every_n`, or `crop` is absent from the current schema, do not supply
+that field; the harness will apply the stage's configured tool policy.
+
+Use these examples as schema templates only. Remove any field that is absent
+from the current stage's tool schema.
+
+Minimal boundary-window request:
+
+```json
+{
+  "start_frame": 67,
+  "end_frame": 91,
+  "reason": "Inspect the local boundary between obs_0004 and obs_0005."
+}
+```
+
+Temporal video request when the schema exposes `mode` and `sample_every_n`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "start_frame": 37,
+  "end_frame": 86,
+  "sample_every_n": 1,
+  "mode": "video",
+  "reason": "Focused inspection of grasp closure and first target motion."
+}
+```
+
+Static comparison request when the schema exposes `tile` mode:
+
+```json
+{
+  "start_frame": 44,
+  "end_frame": 93,
+  "sample_every_n": 7,
+  "mode": "tile",
+  "reason": "Compare target pose before and after the suspected state change."
+}
+```
+
+Local crop request when the schema exposes `crop`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "start_frame": 58,
+  "end_frame": 74,
+  "sample_every_n": 1,
+  "mode": "video",
+  "crop": {
+    "left_pct": 29,
+    "top_pct": 22,
+    "right_pct": 76,
+    "bottom_pct": 83
+  },
+  "reason": "Cropped temporal inspection of the gripper and target contact."
+}
+```
+
+When the current schema exposes `mode`, choose `video` when temporal dynamics
+matter and choose `tile` when static before/during/after comparison is more
+useful. When the current schema exposes `sample_every_n`, prefer
+`sample_every_n=1` for short focused windows, then increase it only when a
+request would exceed `visual.max_attached_frames_per_call`. When the current
+schema exposes `crop`, use it only when the relevant change is local, small,
+subtle, thin, partially occluded, or visually ambiguous.
+
+Do not assume a tool request was inspected if the tool returned an error.
+
+## Task-Relevant Timeline And State Changes
+
+Use semantic intervals, not per-frame micromanagement. Do not split frames
+without a visible semantic change, but localize important semantic boundaries as
+precisely as the visual evidence allows.
+
+Build and audit timelines around task progress, not around equal-length video
+chunks. Separate task-relevant preparation, task-critical state-changing action,
+sustained controlled motion, release, withdrawal, transition, and no-progress
+intervals when they are visually distinct.
+
+Treat approach, alignment, repositioning, or transition as task-relevant
+preparation only when it visibly improves the robot's geometric or operational
+relation to the current required object, region, or control. In a sequential
+task, after one required subgoal is visibly completed and stable, movement,
+alignment, or positioning toward the next required target, region, or control can
+be next-subgoal preparation.
+
+Do not let approach, withdrawal, transition, or generic repositioning absorb the
+boundary of a task-critical action. Critical actions that can make the task
+complete should be their own observation intervals or progress edits when the
+evidence supports that boundary.
+
+Record or account for intervals with no task progress, such as waiting, generic
+or ineffective approach/repositioning, wrong-target or wrong-direction movement,
+failed contact, object remaining stationary without improved
+approach/alignment/control relation, loss of control, or post-failure motion.
+
+When a task-critical attempt fails, compare both the target entity/control state
+and the robot-target readiness relation before and after the attempt. Record or
+account for whether readiness is worse than before, such as an empty closed
+gripper, missed contact, lost alignment, overshoot, unstable contact, or visible
+need to reopen, reposition, or recover.
+
+For small, thin, partially occluded, or visually subtle task-relevant entities or
+controls, do not infer state change from gripper or arm motion alone. A
+high-confidence observation or major progress increase for such an entity/control
+state change requires focused local visual evidence. Use `crop` only when the
+current stage's `inspect_visual` schema exposes it; otherwise use the most
+focused uncropped window available in that stage and lower confidence if the
+entity/control state itself remains unclear.
+
+When text or edit reasons claim that a task-relevant entity/control changed
+state, describe the visible before/after state of that entity/control, not only
+the gripper or arm motion. If the entity/control state change is not directly
+visible, say so, lower confidence, and keep progress conservative.
+
+## Control Acquisition And Outcome Evidence
+
+For tasks where a brief action may establish control, constraint, attachment,
+locking, or support, keep these phases separate whenever they are visually
+distinguishable: setup or approach, the narrow acquisition/control-complete
+boundary, later outcome evidence, and sustained controlled motion. This applies
+to grasping and pick-up cases, and to analogous short events such as hooking,
+latching, inserting until constrained, or making stable support.
+
+The acquisition/control-complete boundary is the earliest supported frame where
+the control relation appears complete. It is not automatically the first later
+frame where the target clearly moves, lifts off, follows the robot, remains
+attached, or otherwise makes the outcome obvious. Later outcome evidence can
+verify or refute the earlier acquisition, but it should be recorded and judged
+separately.
+
+When evidence supports it, expose the acquisition/control-complete boundary as a
+tight 2-frame closed interval such as `[k, k+1]` in observation-writing and
+observation-audit stages. If the boundary is visually ambiguous, record the
+narrowest supported attempt interval, lower confidence, and state the boundary
+uncertainty instead of merging it into setup or later transport.
+
+Do not merge setup with acquisition, or acquisition with outcome evidence, when
+they are visually separable. Phrases such as "approaches and closes", "reaches
+and grasps", "aligns and latches", "moves to and hooks", "contacts and locks",
+"closes and begins to lift", or "the object moves as the grasp is established"
+are warning signs that the interval may need to be split.
+
+Treat visually distinct retries as separate phases. If an initial closure,
+contact, near-enclosure, attachment, lock, or support attempt is not followed by
+stable target motion or the intended task-relevant state change, record it as a
+failed acquisition attempt rather than as generic approach. If the robot then
+reopens, withdraws, or repositions before a later successful attempt, keep the
+failed attempt, recovery/repositioning, later acquisition, and sustained motion
+as separate observations whenever the video supports the distinction.
+
+## Deformable Object State
+
+For deformable-object tasks such as folding, unfolding, flattening, spreading,
+draping, or cloth manipulation, judge visual progress and success by the
+object's visible state relative to the detailed task description. Do not infer
+success merely because the object has been grasped, moved, compressed, bunched,
+or gathered into a pile.
+
+When the task specifies a shape, fold, flatness, coverage, exposure, alignment,
+orientation, placement relation, or support relation, compare the deformable
+object's visible state against that requirement. If the object is wrinkled,
+bunched, twisted, folded in the wrong direction, only partially spread, or
+occluding the required relation, record that mismatch explicitly and lower
+confidence when the exact state is unclear.
+
+## Observations And Confidence
+
+Important visual claims should be recorded through observation tools when those
+tools are available, and tied to an `asset_id` plus a concrete
+`start_frame`/`end_frame` interval.
+
+When using `add_observations` or `revise_observations`, each submitted
+observation or revision must cite `asset_ids` whose frame coverage contains the
+entire submitted closed interval `[start_frame, end_frame]`. If multiple assets
+are cited, their combined coverage must leave no frame gap inside that interval.
+
+Do not cite an asset only because it supports the text claim. The cited asset
+coverage must also cover the observation boundaries and every frame between
+them. If the cited coverage is too narrow, cite additional assets or call
+`inspect_visual` for the missing frames before retrying the observation tool.
+
+Use confidence values consistently:
+
+- `1`: very uncertain;
+- `2`: somewhat uncertain;
+- `3`: moderate confidence;
+- `4`: high confidence;
+- `5`: very high confidence.
+
+Confidence should depend on the clarity of the evidence, not on how plausible
+the task seems from metadata.

+# Bootstrap Observation Stage
+
+Create a precise, task-progress-oriented visual timeline for the whole
+trajectory. The timeline should isolate events that matter for progress, not
+merely narrate equal-length chunks of video.
+
+## Inputs
+
+The runner should attach the full trajectory video at stage start when it fits
+within `visual.max_attached_frames_per_call`. Use that attached video directly
+when it is available. The full-video asset normally has `asset_id="full_video"`
+and covers the original frame sequence without harness-side frame dropping,
+although the file may have been transcoded for model compatibility.
+
+If the full video is unavailable because it exceeds the configured frame limit,
+use `inspect_visual` to request segmented video evidence. Prefer original frame
+rate segments with `sample_every_n=1`; increase `sample_every_n` only when a
+segment would otherwise exceed the frame limit returned by the tool.
+
+If you request segmented evidence, record observations only for segments you
+actually inspected. Do not rely on a failed visual request as evidence.
+
+## Boundary Precision
+
+When `full_video` is attached, treat it as complete frame-level evidence for the
+trajectory. Use the best visible integer frame boundaries from the full video;
+do not treat task-relevant boundaries as coarse samples.
+
+For task-relevant transitions, identify the tightest visible interval you can:
+
+- first visible contact with the task object or control;
+- first controlled object motion;
+- stable grasp or loss of grasp;
+- object leaving or touching a surface;
+- placement, insertion, release, or final stabilization;
+- wrong-object interaction, slip, drop, stall, or recovery.
+
+If a key boundary remains ambiguous because the visual evidence is occluded,
+very fast, or unclear, request a focused `inspect_visual` window around that
+event with `sample_every_n=1` before recording the observation. Use lower
+confidence only when the visual evidence itself is ambiguous.
+
+## Required Work
+
+Record a boundary-aware timeline with `add_observations`.
+
+Use `add_observations` for new observations. If an existing observation needs a
+different boundary, text, or confidence, use `revise_observations` on that
+observation id. Batch multiple additions or revisions together when one visual
+inspection supports them.
+
+Each observation must describe one event interval. Tool frame ranges are closed
+intervals, so `start_frame` and `end_frame` are both included:
+
+```json
+{
+  "asset_ids": ["full_video"],
+  "start_frame": 0,
+  "end_frame": 37,
+  "text": "The gripper approaches the target object; the object remains stationary.",
+  "confidence": 4
+}
+```
+
+Adjacent observations may share exactly one boundary frame when that frame is
+the best visible transition anchor. For example, `[0, 43]` and `[43, 67]` are
+valid neighboring closed intervals. Broader overlaps such as `[0, 48]` and
+`[43, 67]` are invalid.
+
+Guidelines:
+
+- Cover the full trajectory from frame `0` through `metadata["num_frames"] - 1`
+  when `num_frames` is available.
+- Apply the common task-relevant timeline, state-change, terminal-truncation,
+  and control-acquisition rules when creating observations.
+- Keep observation text concrete and visual. Avoid vague claims such as "looks
+  good", "the robot is doing the task", or "probably successful".
+
+After observations are recorded, call `complete_stage()`. The harness will
+return `status="blocked"` if the current observations do not cover the full
+trajectory or if their closed frame intervals overlap by more than one shared
+boundary frame. If completion reports overlap, call `read_observations()` and
+use its `data` field to get the current observation ids, then use
+`revise_observations` to fix the overlapping boundaries. Single-frame endpoint
+sharing is reported as `shared_boundaries`, not as a blocking overlap.
