+# Observation Audit and Challenge Stage
+
+Audit and challenge the candidate observation timeline.
+
+Bootstrap/proposal observations are candidate visual claims, not conclusions.
+Assume they may contain serious errors. In particular, adjacent time boundaries
+may be far from the real visual transition, intervals may be too coarse, and
+some boundaries may be numerically tidy guesses rather than actual task state
+changes. Do not start by looking for reasons to agree with the proposal. Your
+first job is to challenge each current observation against new visual evidence,
+strongly prefer revision when the evidence does not precisely support the
+proposal, and confirm only the observations that survive that audit.
+Treat bootstrap observations as especially suspect when they resemble an
+expected sequence implied by the robot instruction rather than directly verified
+visual events.
+
+## Required Audit Decisions
+
+Use `read_observations()` to see the current observations, draft ids, and
+coverage diagnostics. Every current observation must become `confirmed` before
+this stage can complete.
+
+For every current observation, make one of these audit decisions before calling
+any confirmation tool:
+
+- `as-is`: the current frame range, text, and confidence are supported;
+- `needs boundary revision`: the start or end frame is too early or too late;
+- `needs split`: the observation mixes multiple task-progress phases that
+  should be separated;
+- `needs merge`: two or more adjacent observations are actually one continuous
+  task-progress phase with no meaningful visible boundary between them;
+- `wrong text`: the frame range is usable, but the text or confidence is wrong.
+
+Only `as-is` observations may be confirmed. For the other decisions, use
+`revise_observations`, use `add_observations` as needed when a split creates
+additional intervals, and use `merge_observations` when adjacent observations
+should become one interval.
+
+## Required Visual Challenge
+
+Before confirming an observation, request new `inspect_visual` evidence in this
+stage. Bootstrap/source assets from earlier stages are not valid confirmation
+evidence in this stage, even when the current observation was originally drafted
+from them. Each confirmation must cite a new `asset_id` returned by
+`inspect_visual` during `challenge_observations`.
+
+For observation `[s, e]`, use `start_frame < s` when possible and
+`end_frame > e` when possible; clamp only at the trajectory boundaries. The
+audit evidence should let you challenge:
+
+- the visual claim inside the observation interval;
+- the start boundary, including evidence just before the interval when earlier
+  frames exist;
+- the end boundary, including evidence just after the interval when later frames
+  exist.
+
+Challenge each observation with new visual evidence, then either confirm it
+as-is, revise it, split it, or merge it with adjacent observations.
+
+Do not preserve a proposed boundary because it is numerically tidy. Boundaries
+at multiples of 5 or 10 are especially suspicious unless focused visual
+evidence shows that the actual state change happens there. Prefer concrete
+visual changes such as contact, control acquisition, control completion, target
+motion, target state change, or a clear task-progress phase transition.
+
+For a long observation, do not only inspect the two outer boundaries. Also check
+whether the interval hides an internal task-progress-relevant transition that
+should become its own observation.
+
+For approach, alignment, repositioning, or transition observations, apply the
+common task-relevant timeline rules and challenge whether the motion qualifies as
+preparation. Generic, ineffective, wrong-target, or wrong-direction motion should
+not be confirmed as task-relevant preparation.
+
+Apply the common control-acquisition rules before confirming. Challenge whether
+the timeline exposes a separate setup interval, a narrow
+acquisition/control-complete boundary suitable for downstream 2-frame progress
+credit, later outcome evidence, and any sustained motion or retry phases. Treat
+merged setup/acquisition, acquisition/outcome, or failed-retry/successful-retry
+intervals as `needs split` unless focused visual evidence shows the phases are
+not visually distinguishable. Request focused temporal evidence across suspected
+first attempts, reopen/reposition phases, and later successful attempts when that
+distinction could change the audit. When the current tool schema allows sampling
+control, prefer dense sampling for these short windows.
+
+Clip the request to the valid trajectory range. If the returned evidence uses
+sparse sampling, make sure it still visibly checks the observation interior and
+both available outside-boundary sides. Use `crop` when the current tool schema
+exposes it and the observation depends on a small, subtle, thin, partially
+occluded, or visually ambiguous task-relevant entity/control changing state.
+
+Use `confirm_observations` only after the new visual evidence supports the
+`as-is` decision for the current observation boundaries, text, and confidence.
+Batch multiple `as-is` confirmations together when the same challenge-stage
+inspection supports them.
+
+## When To Revise Or Merge
+
+Use `revise_observations` if the current observation has the wrong frame range,
+wrong text, wrong confidence, or merges phases that should not be merged.
+Use `merge_observations` if adjacent observations split one continuous phase
+only because the proposal used a coarse or arbitrary boundary.
+
+Common reasons to revise:
+
+- the proposal boundary is coarse, arbitrary, or numerically tidy with no
+  matching visual transition;
+- adjacent time boundaries are far from the real visual transition;
+- an observation is too coarse and should be narrowed around the actual
+  task-progress change, including when it hides an internal key boundary;
+- approach/preparation and task-critical action are in the same observation;
+- task-critical action and withdrawal/transition are in the same observation;
+- setup, acquisition/control-complete boundary, outcome evidence, or sustained
+  motion are merged even though the common control-acquisition rules require
+  separate intervals;
+- a failed first attempt, recovery/repositioning, and later successful attempt
+  are merged into one approach or acquisition interval;
+- approach, alignment, or repositioning motion is mislabeled as task-relevant
+  preparation or generic no-progress motion;
+- the text infers task success from arm or gripper motion without visible
+  target entity/control state evidence;
+- the text treats a simulator-truncated terminal video as partial success only
+  because no post-success dwell frames are visible;
+- the confidence is too high for the available visual evidence.
+
+Common reasons to merge:
+
+- adjacent observations describe the same preparation, approach, alignment,
+  acquisition, motion, outcome, or no-progress phase;
+- the only apparent boundary between adjacent observations is an arbitrary
+  numerical cut rather than a visible task-progress transition;
+- the text changes but the visible task-progress state does not;
+- the proposed split would create fake downstream progress credit at a frame
+  where no meaningful visual transition occurs.
+
+If one observation should be split, revise the original observation into the
+first resulting interval, then use `add_observations` for the remaining intervals.
+All revised or newly added observations are draft observations and must be
+confirmed with challenge-stage visual evidence before this stage can complete.
+When revising or adding split intervals, apply the common observation tool
+evidence-coverage rule to every submitted interval.
+
+All merged observations are also draft observations. After calling
+`merge_observations`, inspect the merged interval and available outside-boundary
+context, then confirm the merged observation only if the new evidence supports
+its full frame range, text, and confidence.
+
+## Coverage
+
+The current observations must cover the full trajectory with closed intervals.
+No frame gaps are allowed. Adjacent observations may share exactly one boundary
+frame, such as `[0, 43]` and `[43, 67]`, when that frame is the best visible
+transition anchor. Broader overlaps are not allowed.
+
+Use `read_observations()` after revisions when you need to check the remaining
+draft ids, gaps, shared boundaries, or overlaps.
+
+When all observations are confirmed and coverage is complete, call
+`complete_stage()`. If completion returns `status="blocked"`, follow the
+returned `blocked_items` and `next_required_actions`.

+# Progress Stage
+
+Audit or generate the progress curve using progress information provided at
+stage start and the observation timeline when available.
+
+## Stage Start
+
+Use observations supplied in the stage context or returned by
+`read_observations` when they are available.
+
+The runner should also provide an initial `progress_snapshot` and
+`progress_summary` for this stage. Use them as the starting point for progress
+audit or generation. `read_progress` and `summarize_progress` remain available
+for local rechecks, especially after edits.
+
+In this stage's Case context, `progress_state` is only a compact status summary.
+The runner-provided `progress_snapshot` contains the frame-level progress rows.
+
+`progress_snapshot` tells you whether candidate progress rows are present:
+
+- If `has_progress_proposal=true`, your mode is `audit_and_correct_candidate_progress`. Verify the proposal and edit unsupported values.
+- If `has_progress_proposal=false`, your mode is `generate_progress_from_visual_evidence`. You must assign all frames before export.
+
+Treat proposal values as candidates to verify, not as ground truth.
+
+## Internal Plan
+
+Before editing, form a short internal plan:
+
+- What robot instruction was sent?
+- Which available observation intervals mark task-relevant state changes?
+- Which candidate progress jumps or suspicious intervals need checking?
+- Which progress rows or segments need correction or generation?
+- Whether any progress-critical boundary still needs a final visual recheck.
+
+Do not output a long plan unless it helps the final result. Use the plan to
+guide tool calls.
+
+## Optional Focused Recheck
+
+When observations are available, use them as the main structure for progress.
+You may still call `inspect_visual` for a focused recheck when a candidate jump,
+subtle state change, or final completion judgment would materially change the
+curve.
+
+When using observations, respect their boundaries. Do not invent a new internal
+progress boundary that contradicts the observation timeline unless you have just
+inspected focused evidence and the final summary explicitly reports that the
+observations were insufficient for that finer split. When in doubt, keep
+progress edits aligned with observation intervals.
+
+For subtle target-entity/control changes, an uncropped full-frame clip alone is
+not sufficient evidence for a high-confidence major progress increase. If
+available observations do not already include focused local evidence, request a
+focused `inspect_visual` asset using only the arguments exposed in this stage's
+tool schema before assigning that major increase.
+
+Follow the common Visual Inspection Tool schema rules. In this stage, when the
+schema exposes `mode`, prefer `mode="video"` for candidate jumps whose timing
+matters and `mode="tile"` for before/during/after state comparison. Use `crop`
+only if the current schema exposes it.
+
+When the observation supports a progress increase, explicitly describe the
+task-relevant entity/control state before and after the interval. Do not infer
+success from gripper or arm motion alone. If the target entity/control state
+change is not directly visible after focused inspection, lower confidence and
+avoid claiming high progress for that state change.
+
+Avoid vague observations such as:
+
+- "Looks good."
+- "The robot is doing the task."
+- "Probably successful."
+- "The reward seems right."
+
+Do not call observation-writing tools in this stage; they are not available.
+If the observation timeline is unavailable or insufficient, use focused visual
+evidence where needed rather than inventing unsupported visual facts.
+
+## Candidate Evaluation
+
+When candidate progress is present, compare it against visual evidence:
+
+- If candidate values increase during task-relevant preparation, the increase
+  should be modest. Generic, ineffective, or wrong-target preparation should
+  stay flat; preparation that damages an already achieved task relation may
+  justify a small regression.
+- Large increases should align with visible task-relevant state changes, not
+  merely with robot motion or with a state that was already achieved before the
+  interval.
+- For subtle entity/control changes, require direct evidence that the
+  task-relevant entity/control itself changed state. Hand, gripper, or arm
+  motion near the target is not enough by itself.
+- A major increase for a subtle entity/control change requires supporting
+  focused local visual evidence. Without that asset, reduce confidence
+  and keep the progress increase modest even if the full-frame video appears
+  plausible.
+- A high final score should require visible completion, with stability judged
+  from available evidence. For simulator-truncated terminal videos, a visibly
+  achieved final task condition at the last frames can justify high final
+  progress even without extra post-success dwell frames.
+- Regressing progress should be assigned when the robot manipulates the wrong object, loses control, stalls, or fails to change the required task-relevant state. Use a plateau only when the interval preserves the same useful task-relevant state and does not move the robot farther from the required next subgoal.
+- Do not use tiny positive deltas to acknowledge effort on a wrong object; wrong-object manipulation is flat at best and usually regressing.
+- Repeated same attempts, unusually long approach, unusually long holding, or
+  visible stalling without a new task-relevant state improvement should be
+  treated as local regression, especially when the robot is no closer to a
+  useful target relation than before the interval.
+- Sparse candidate annotations should be judged by their stated frame ranges or nearest visible intervals.
+
+Do not collapse all progress to zero merely because the final task fails.
+Modest progress may be appropriate for task-relevant preparation.
+Keep preparation-phase values low and conservative because the central task
+state has not changed yet.
+
+The configured progress value range is
+`[{{progress_value_min_points}}, {{progress_value_max_points}}]`. Avoid
+over-interpreting tiny numeric differences. Focus on relative shape, temporal
+alignment, and support from visible events.
+
+Use `summarize_progress` to recheck candidate jumps after edits or when the
+initial summary is insufficient. Use `read_progress(..., include_edit_spans=true)`
+after edits to verify that the current curve matches your intended corrections.
+
+## Subgoal Progress Scale
+
+For sequential robot instructions, identify the visible, verifiable subgoals
+implied by the instruction before assigning high progress. If the instruction
+contains $N$ such subgoals, then the progress value at the moment the $n$-th
+subgoal becomes visibly completed should not exceed $n/N$ of the configured
+progress range.
+
+After the $n$-th subgoal is completed but before the $(n+1)$-th subgoal is
+completed, progress may increase for visible preparation, approach, or attempts
+toward the next subgoal, but it should remain below the $(n+1)/N$ completion
+level. Treat the interval $[n/N, (n+1)/N)$ as "the first $n$ subgoals are
+complete, and the trajectory is attempting the next subgoal."
+
+## Reward/Progress Judgment Guidance
+
+Base the judgment on task-relevant state transitions:
+
+- task-relevant preparation without object/control state change: modest progress
+  or weak positive reward at most;
+- generic, ineffective, wrong-target, wrong-direction, repeated, or unusually
+  slow preparation: local regression unless it is a brief reasonable hold that
+  visibly preserves an already useful task relation;
+- stable contact but no control: still conservative;
+- transition from no reliable control to stable control, followed by a first
+  task-relevant state change such as lift-off, separation, actuation, or initial
+  displacement: a substantial local progress increase can be justified;
+- sustained carrying, transport, adjustment, or continued controlled motion
+  after control is already established: progress should usually increase
+  gradually according to visible advancement toward the target relation or final
+  state;
+- correct placement, insertion, or final configuration: high progress can be
+  justified if stable in the available evidence or visibly terminally satisfied
+  at the video endpoint;
+- wrong object, wrong direction, drop, or unstable final state: assign a local progress decrease for the affected interval; final progress should reflect only the strongest required task state still preserved after the failure.
+
+Do not reward time passing, camera motion, or visually impressive robot movement
+unless it advances the task.
+
+For deformable-object tasks, apply the common deformable-object-state rule
+before assigning high progress or final completion. A bunched, twisted,
+wrongly folded, partially spread, or otherwise task-mismatched object should
+stay below completion-level progress even if it has been manipulated.
+
+Apply the common control-acquisition rules when assigning progress for brief
+control, constraint, attachment, locking, or support events. Treat verified
+acquisition as a temporally localized event, not as generic preparation or later
+transport. Assign progress with these rules:
+
+- Setup, approach, pose adjustment, and alignment should receive gradual,
+  modest progress only when they visibly improve readiness for the target
+  entity or control.
+- The brief acquisition action is a task-critical attempt. Do not give the main
+  acquisition jump merely because the gripper closes, contact occurs, a tool
+  touches, or the target becomes occluded.
+- Use later outcome frames to judge whether the attempt actually established
+  control or constraint, then assign the main progress jump retrospectively to
+  the earliest supportable acquisition/control-complete boundary. Do not move
+  the main acquisition credit to a later lift, pull, carry, transport, or first
+  obvious target-motion frame merely because that frame verifies success more
+  clearly.
+- The 2-frame acquisition interval should be its own progress edit with
+  `end_frame = start_frame + 1`. Choose the best visible boundary near the
+  completion of closure, locking, attachment, or equivalent acquisition. Choose
+  `[k, k+1]` at the first obvious target-motion frame only when no earlier
+  control-complete boundary can be supported after focused inspection, and state
+  that uncertainty in the edit reason.
+- Treat this as a hard editing constraint for major acquisition credit. If an
+  acquisition-related edit changes progress by at least
+  `{{progress_default_jump_threshold_points}}` points, that edit must be the
+  tight 2-frame acquisition edit. A longer edit whose reason is "grasp",
+  "acquisition", "control established", "locked", "attached", or equivalent
+  should be only setup/preparation or post-acquisition gradual motion, not the
+  main acquisition jump.
+- If the observation timeline merges setup and acquisition, do not use the whole
+  observation as the acquisition edit. Use the available evidence and, if
+  needed, one focused `inspect_visual` request to locate the best 2-frame
+  acquisition boundary. If no boundary can be supported, keep the
+  acquisition credit below the major-jump threshold and state the uncertainty
+  instead of smearing a large jump over the merged interval.
+- After verified acquisition, immediate lift-off, separation, pull-away, height,
+  transport, carrying, or other sustained controlled motion should receive only
+  additional gradual progress for the visible advancement that happens after
+  control has already been acquired.
+- If later outcome evidence refutes the attempt, such as an empty closed
+  gripper, slip, drop, object left behind, unlocked relation, failed attachment,
+  or visible need to reopen, retry, or recover, do not treat the acquisition
+  attempt as successful progress. Keep it flat or assign a local regression
+  according to the remaining readiness and target-entity state.
+- If the later outcome is absent or still ambiguous, keep acquisition credit
+  conservative and describe the uncertainty rather than forcing a high jump.
+
+For ineffective task-critical attempts, compare both the target entity/control
+state and the robot-target readiness relation before and after the attempt. If
+the robot attempts a task-critical action such as grasping, pushing, pulling,
+inserting, placing, pressing, switching, or actuating, but fails to produce the
+intended task-relevant state change, do not treat the attempt itself as
+progress. If the failed attempt leaves the robot less ready than before, such as
+an empty closed gripper, missed contact, lost alignment, overshoot, unstable
+contact, or a visible need to reopen, reposition, or recover, assign a mild
+local regression with `end_progress_points` lower than
+`start_progress_points`. If the failed attempt also worsens the target
+entity/control state, such as moving it away from the goal, disturbing
+alignment, causing slip or drop, reversing actuation, destabilizing placement,
+or breaking a completed subgoal, assign a stronger local regression. Keep the
+curve flat only when the failed attempt visibly preserves the same or better
+useful readiness relation as before. Post-failure progress should reflect the
+strongest task-relevant state still visibly preserved after the attempt, not the
+robot's effort.
+
+For next-subgoal preparation in sequential tasks, keep the increase smaller
+than the progress assigned to actually contacting, controlling, transporting,
+placing, inserting, actuating, releasing, or stabilizing the next task-relevant
+entity/control. Do not give next-subgoal preparation progress when the available
+evidence says the previous subgoal is not yet stable or the motion breaks a
+previously achieved task relation.
+
+For small or subtle state changes, base the progress judgment on the target
+entity/control itself: compare its visible pose, configuration, contact/support
+relation, or actuation state before and after the interval. If the target state
+change cannot be seen clearly, do not assign a high-confidence major increase
+even if the gripper motion looks plausible.
+
+For those small or subtle state changes, "seen clearly" means the relevant
+local region has been inspected with `crop`; a full-frame
+clip by itself is not enough to justify a high-confidence major increase.
+
+Do not assign the main progress increase for a prior subgoal to a later
+withdrawal, release, lift-away, or transition-to-next-target interval. Judge
+only the new task-relevant relation that improves inside the edited interval.
+Such post-action transition intervals should usually be plateaus or modest
+preparation increases unless the withdrawal or release itself visibly creates
+or stabilizes the required task state.
+
+For failure cases, do not stretch the interpretation toward success. State the
+strongest visible achievement and where the trajectory stops making
+task-relevant progress. A failed trajectory can still have a nonzero curve if it
+visibly reaches an approach, alignment, contact, partial manipulation, or other
+task-relevant intermediate state.
+
+## Progress Editing And Generation
+
+Use `edit_progress_segments` for local event-timed progress edits and
+`calibrate_progress_curve` for trajectory-level affine calibration from two
+explicit frame/value anchors.
+
+`edit_progress_segments` applies one or more local segment edits in a single
+call. Each segment linearly interpolates between two typed endpoint values:
+`start_progress_points` at `start_frame` and `end_progress_points` at
+`end_frame`. Use this to capture gradual, fine-grained increases or decreases
+across visually meaningful intervals, including small approach improvements,
+alignment changes, controlled motion, brief regressions, slips, or recovery.
+Inside each segment, do not pass JSON arrays or strings for progress values.
+
+When building adjacent piecewise segments, share the boundary frame instead of
+leaving a one-frame gap between segment endpoints. For example, use `[0, 43]`
+and `[43, 67]`, not `[0, 42]` and `[43, 67]`, when frame `43` is the semantic
+anchor between the two progress trends. The shared boundary frame should have
+the same progress value in both adjacent segment entries. Segments in one batch
+must already be ordered and may not overlap beyond that single shared frame.
+
+For a plateau, set `start_progress_points` equal to `end_progress_points`. For a
+small regression, set `end_progress_points` lower than `start_progress_points`.
+The returned edit record automatically reports the segment `trend` as
+`increase`, `flat`, or `decrease` from those endpoint values; do not pass
+`trend` as an input.
+
+For candidate proposals:
+
+- Keep proposal values where visible evidence supports them.
+- Edit local unsupported intervals instead of rewriting the whole curve by default.
+- `edit_progress_segments` only supports local `propagation="none"` edits. If a later baseline is wrong, explicitly rewrite the affected later intervals.
+- Prefer evidence-grounded segment edits over per-frame micromanagement.
+
+For no-proposal cases:
+
+- Generate a complete current progress curve from visual evidence.
+- Use broad piecewise segments: low/flat before task-relevant behavior, modest approach or preparation progress, stronger increases around key task-relevant achievements, and high values only for visibly complete terminal task states.
+- All frames must be assigned before export.
+
+## Affine Calibration Guidance
+
+Use `calibrate_progress_curve` when the current curve's relative trend is
+credible, but two key frames should correspond to clearer semantic progress
+values. Typical anchors include the start frame mapping to 0, a frame where the
+$n$-th subgoal becomes completed mapping to at most $n/N$ of the configured
+range, or a failure endpoint mapping back to the strongest subgoal state still
+visibly preserved.
+
+The tool applies one affine transform to assigned current-progress rows only.
+Unassigned rows remain unassigned. Both anchor frames must already be assigned,
+and the tool blocks without changing the curve if the anchors would require a
+negative scale or if any transformed assigned row would leave the configured
+progress range.
+
+Do not use `calibrate_progress_curve` when a local peak, jump, plateau, or
+regression is placed at the wrong frame; when wrong-object manipulation,
+failed attempts, empty grasps, drops, or slips are incorrectly rewarded; or
+when the relative trend between the anchors is not credible. Fix those issues
+first with `edit_progress_segments`.
+
+Every `edit_progress_segments` segment must include:
+
+- `start_progress_points` and `end_progress_points`, integers in
+  `[{{progress_value_min_points}}, {{progress_value_max_points}}]`;
+- a concrete evidence-grounded reason;
+- the relevant closed frame range;
+- a confidence value in `[1, 5]`.
+
+Every `calibrate_progress_curve` call must include two assigned frame/value
+anchors, a concrete evidence-grounded reason, and a confidence value in
+`[1, 5]`. Reasons may refer to observation intervals, focused visual
+assets, or visible events. They do not need to mechanically cite an observation
+id.
+
+Do not set final progress near `{{progress_value_max_points}}` unless the
+final task condition is visibly complete and either stable in the available
+frames or terminally satisfied at the video endpoint. Lack of additional frames
+after a visible terminal success should not be treated as partial success by
+itself. If the trajectory only reaches an intermediate state and then fails,
+final progress should reflect that strongest visible intermediate achievement
+rather than dropping automatically to zero or stretching toward completion.
+Validation treats a final progress value below
+`{{progress_value_max_points}}` as an incomplete terminal curve.
+
+Once available evidence establishes the main task outcome, make progress edits
+promptly. Do not continue requesting visual evidence if existing evidence
+already supports the needed correction or generated segment.
+
+## When To Stop Inspecting
+
+You usually have enough evidence when:
+
+- the robot instruction is clear;
+- available observations, if any, identify the main trajectory structure;
+- focused clips or tiles, when needed, cover any remaining key success/failure transitions;
+- progress values have been corrected or generated with `edit_progress_segments` and any needed `calibrate_progress_curve`;
+- all progress rows are assigned;
+- `validate_progress()` returns `ok=true`;
+- a final summary for the validated progress curve has been written with `write_summary`;
+- remaining uncertainty would not change the main conclusion.
+
+If uncertainty would change the conclusion, request one more focused visual
+artifact before finalizing.
+
+## Finalization
+
+Required final tool order:
+
+```text
+edit_progress_segments(...)  # one call with one or more segments, unless the proposal is fully supported
+calibrate_progress_curve(...)  # optional, only when two semantic anchors justify a global affine calibration
+validate_progress()
+write_summary(...)
+complete_stage()
+```
+
+If the proposal is fully supported and no edit is needed, still call
+`validate_progress()`, `write_summary()`, and `complete_stage()`.
+
+Only call `write_summary()` after `validate_progress()` returns `ok=true`.
+If `validate_progress()` returns `ok=false` with `status="blocked"`, follow the
+returned `blocked_items` and `next_required_actions`, fix the curve with
+`edit_progress_segments` or `calibrate_progress_curve` as appropriate, and call
+`validate_progress()` again before writing the summary.
+A blocked `write_summary()` means the summary was not accepted; resolve the
+reported issue, and retry.
+
+The `summary` passed to `write_summary` should be Markdown and include:
+
+- robot instruction;
+- progress mode: `audit_and_correct_candidate_progress` or `generate_progress_from_visual_evidence`;
+- whether candidate progress was present;
+- observations, if any, and any focused visual evidence inspected, with `asset_id` and closed frame ranges;
+- progress edits or generated segments, with closed frame ranges;
+- main reward/progress judgment;
+- evidence supporting that judgment;
+- candidate mismatches, if any.
+
+You may have made mistakes even if your analysis seems convincing. Use the
+`external_review_need` passed to `write_summary` to rate how much this result
+needs independent external review, based on the limits of your own ability and
+how difficult the video was for you to understand. Do not base the rating on
+whether the trajectory succeeded or failed. `1` means no external review is
+needed; `5` means external review is strongly needed.
+
+If review is needed, use `external_review_focus` to state briefly what the
+reviewer should check. Otherwise omit `external_review_focus`.
+
+Use `candidate_supported: null` when no candidate progress proposal is present
+or when the proposal cannot be evaluated from the available evidence.
+
+Use `candidate_progress_present: false` and
+`progress_mode: "generate_progress_from_visual_evidence"` when no candidate
+progress proposal is present.
+
+Call `complete_stage()` after `write_summary()`. If it returns `ok=false` with
+`status="blocked"`, follow the returned `blocked_items` and
+`next_required_actions`, fix the curve or rewrite the summary as requested, and
+call the relevant validation/finalization tool again.

+def split_contiguous_episode_indices(
+    episode_indices: Sequence[int],
+    *,
+    num_nodes: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]:
+    """Split one ordered schedule into contiguous shards differing by at most one."""
+
+    if isinstance(num_nodes, bool) or not isinstance(num_nodes, int) or num_nodes <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"num_nodes must be a positive integer, got {num_nodes!r}.")
+    ordered = tuple(int(index) for index in episode_indices)
+    if len(ordered) < num_nodes:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Ray run-batch requires at least one episode per node: "
+            f"episodes={len(ordered)}, num_nodes={num_nodes}."
+        )
+
+    base_size, remainder = divmod(len(ordered), num_nodes)
+    shards: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
+    start = 0
+    for node_rank in range(num_nodes):
+        shard_size = base_size + (1 if node_rank < remainder else 0)
+        stop = start + shard_size
+        shards.append(ordered[start:stop])
+        start = stop
+    return tuple(shards)
+
+
+def eligible_ray_nodes(
+    raw_nodes: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    *,
+    required_gpus_per_node: int,
+) -> list[RayNodeSpec]:
+    """Filter alive GPU-capable nodes and return them in stable IP order."""
+
+    selected_by_id: dict[str, RayNodeSpec] = {}
+    for raw_node in raw_nodes:
+        if raw_node.get("Alive") is not True:
+            continue
+        resources = raw_node.get("Resources") or {}
+        if not isinstance(resources, Mapping):
+            continue
+        gpu_capacity = float(resources.get("GPU", 0.0))
+        if gpu_capacity < float(required_gpus_per_node):
+            continue
+        node_id = str(raw_node.get("NodeID") or "").strip()
+        node_ip = str(raw_node.get("NodeManagerAddress") or "").strip()
+        if not node_id or not node_ip:
+            continue
+        selected_by_id[node_id] = RayNodeSpec(
+            node_id=node_id,
+            node_ip=node_ip,
+            gpu_capacity=gpu_capacity,
+        )
+    return sorted(selected_by_id.values(), key=_ray_node_sort_key)
+

+def wait_for_ray_nodes(
+    ray_module: Any,
+    *,
+    num_nodes: int,
+    required_gpus_per_node: int,
+    timeout_seconds: float,
+    poll_interval_seconds: float = 2.0,
+) -> list[RayNodeSpec]:
+    """Wait until the platform-started Ray cluster exposes enough GPU nodes."""
+
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + float(timeout_seconds)
+    last_eligible: list[RayNodeSpec] = []
+    while True:
+        last_eligible = eligible_ray_nodes(
+            ray_module.nodes(),
+            required_gpus_per_node=required_gpus_per_node,
+        )
+        if len(last_eligible) >= num_nodes:
+            return last_eligible[:num_nodes]
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            visible = [node.to_dict() for node in last_eligible]
+            raise TimeoutError(
+                "Timed out waiting for Ray GPU nodes: "
+                f"required_nodes={num_nodes}, "
+                f"required_gpus_per_node={required_gpus_per_node}, "
+                f"eligible_nodes={visible}."
+            )
+        time.sleep(float(poll_interval_seconds))

+        else:

+                "port_preflight": port_preflight_by_rank.get(plan.node_rank),

+            "actual_ray_node_id": actual_node_id,
+            "ray_assigned_gpu_ids": [int(gpu_id) for gpu_id in assigned_gpu_ids],
+            **managed_port_system_context(),
+        }
+        try:
+            reservations = reserve_managed_server_ports(server_endpoints)
+        except ManagedServerPortUnavailableError as exc:
+            # Expected bind collisions are returned as data so the driver can
+            # preserve the exact endpoint and port in distributed_summary.json.
+            payload = {
+                **base_payload,
+                "status": "failed",
+                "server_port_allocations": [
+                    endpoint.port_allocation_dict()
+                    for endpoint in server_endpoints
+                ],
+                "failure": exc.to_dict(),
+            }
+            self._port_preflight_payload = payload
+            return dict(payload)
+
+        self._preflight_server_endpoints = server_endpoints
+        self._preflight_gpu_id_map = gpu_id_map
+        self._port_reservations = reservations
+        payload = {
+            **base_payload,
+            "status": "passed",
+            "server_port_allocations": [
+                endpoint.port_allocation_dict() for endpoint in server_endpoints
+            ],
+            "failure": None,
+        }
+        self._port_preflight_payload = payload
+        return dict(payload)
+
+    def prepare(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Map Ray GPUs, start every configured local server, and wait ready."""
+
+        if self._manager is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.node_name} has already been prepared.")
+
+        actual_node_id, assigned_gpu_ids = self._runtime_assignment()
+        if (
+            self._preflight_server_endpoints is None
+            or self._preflight_gpu_id_map is None
+            or self._port_reservations is None
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"{self.node_name} must pass check_server_ports() before prepare()."
+            )
+        server_endpoints = self._preflight_server_endpoints
+        gpu_id_map = self._preflight_gpu_id_map
+        startup_config = resolve_server_startup_config(
+            self.server_payload.get("startup")
+        )
+
+        config_payload = dict(self.config_payload)
+        batch_payload = dict(config_payload.get("batch") or {})
+        batch_payload["episode_indices"] = list(self.episode_indices)
+        config_payload["batch"] = batch_payload
+        shard_config = RewardAgentConfig.from_dict(config_payload)
+        if shard_config.vllm.endpoint_groups:
+            client_endpoints = resolve_client_endpoint_groups(
+                list(shard_config.vllm.endpoint_groups)
+            )
+        else:
+            client_endpoints = derive_client_endpoints_from_server(
+                server_endpoints,
+                max_concurrent=self.max_concurrent_per_endpoint,
+            )
+        validate_client_server_alignment(
+            client_endpoints=client_endpoints,
+            server_endpoints=server_endpoints,
+        )
+
+        manager = ServingManager(
+            client_endpoints,
+            server_endpoints=server_endpoints,
+            startup_config=startup_config,
+            port_reservations=self._port_reservations,
+        )
+        # Ownership transfers to ServingManager even if startup later fails.
+        self._port_reservations = None
+        batch_runner = RewardAgentBatchRunner(
+            lerobot_root=self.lerobot_root,
+            output_root=self.nodes_output_root,
+            config=shard_config,
+            serving_manager=manager,
+            batch_id=self.node_name,
+            proposal_batch_results=self.proposal_batch_results,
+            check_server_ready=False,
+            print_context=self.print_context,
+        )
+        try:
+            prepared_batch = batch_runner.prepare()
+            _write_json(
+                prepared_batch.workspace.batch_dir / "shard_plan.json",
+                self.shard_plan,
+            )
+            manager.set_log_dir(prepared_batch.workspace.servers_dir)
+        except Exception:
+            # Input/workspace preflight happens before Popen, but the manager
+            # already owns the cross-node port reservations and must release them.
+            manager.shutdown()
+            raise
+
+        try:
+            manager.start_managed()
+        except Exception as exc:
+            try:
+                _write_json(
+                    self.node_dir / "server_failure.json",
+                    {
+                        "node_rank": self.node_rank,
+                        "node_name": self.node_name,
+                        "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
+                        "error": str(exc),
+                        "startup": startup_config.to_dict(),
+                        "server_endpoints": [
+                            endpoint.to_dict() for endpoint in server_endpoints
+                        ],
+                    },
+                )
+            finally:
+                manager.shutdown()
+            raise
+
+        self._manager = manager
+        self._gpu_id_map = gpu_id_map
+        self._batch_runner = batch_runner
+        self._prepared_batch = prepared_batch
+        try:
+            runtime_payload = {
+                "node_rank": self.node_rank,
+                "node_name": self.node_name,
+                "expected_ray_node_id": self.expected_ray_node_id,
+                "actual_ray_node_id": actual_node_id,
+                "ray_assigned_gpu_ids": [int(gpu_id) for gpu_id in assigned_gpu_ids],
+                "logical_to_assigned_gpu_id": {
+                    str(logical): int(assigned)
+                    for logical, assigned in sorted(gpu_id_map.items())
+                },
+                "episode_indices": list(self.episode_indices),
+                "server_startup": startup_config.to_dict(),
+                "server_endpoints": [
+                    endpoint.to_dict() for endpoint in server_endpoints
+                ],
+            }
+            _write_json(self.node_dir / "ray_runtime.json", runtime_payload)
+            _write_json(
+                self.node_dir / "server_status.json",
+                {
+                    "status": "ready",
+                    "startup": startup_config.to_dict(),
+                    "server_endpoints": [
+                        endpoint.to_dict() for endpoint in server_endpoints
+                    ],
+                },
+            )
+        except Exception:
+            # Once the manager is attached to the actor, any metadata failure
+            # must still stop the already-ready node-local server processes.
+            self._shutdown_manager()
+            raise
+        return runtime_payload
+
+    def run_shard(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Run the existing node-local batch scheduler for this fixed shard."""
+
+        if (
+            self._manager is None
+            or self._batch_runner is None
+            or self._prepared_batch is None
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.node_name} must be prepared before run_shard().")
+
+        try:
+            batch = self._batch_runner.run(self._prepared_batch)
+            shard_summary = json.loads(
+                batch.batch_summary.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+            )
+            return {
+                "node_rank": self.node_rank,
+                "node_name": self.node_name,
+                "status": "completed",
+                "batch_dir": str(batch.batch_dir),
+                "batch_results": str(batch.batch_results),
+                "batch_events": str(batch.batch_events),
+                "batch_summary": str(batch.batch_summary),
+                "serving_resolved": str(batch.serving_resolved),
+                "total_episodes": int(batch.total_episodes),
+                "terminal_result_count": int(
+                    shard_summary.get("terminal_result_count", 0)
+                ),
+                "status_counts": dict(shard_summary.get("status_counts") or {}),
+            }
+        finally:
+            self._shutdown_manager()
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Best-effort explicit cleanup used by the driver on every exit path."""
+
+        self._shutdown_manager()
+        return {
+            "node_rank": self.node_rank,
+            "node_name": self.node_name,
+            "shutdown": True,
+        }
+
+    def _shutdown_manager(self) -> None:
+        """Release reservations and local server processes exactly once."""
+
+        reservations = self._port_reservations
+        self._port_reservations = None
+        if reservations is not None:
+            reservations.close()
+        manager = self._manager
+        self._manager = None
+        self._batch_runner = None
+        self._prepared_batch = None
+        if manager is not None:
+            manager.shutdown()
+
+    def _runtime_assignment(self) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]:
+        """Return and validate the Ray node/GPU assignment for this actor."""
+
+        # Ray remains optional for the normal local run-batch path because it
+        # is imported only inside methods executed by a Ray actor.
+        import ray
+
+        runtime_context = ray.get_runtime_context()
+        actual_node_id = str(runtime_context.get_node_id())
+        if actual_node_id != self.expected_ray_node_id:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"{self.node_name} was scheduled on Ray node {actual_node_id}, "
+                f"expected {self.expected_ray_node_id}."
+            )
+        return actual_node_id, list(ray.get_gpu_ids())
+
+    def _resolve_server_layout(
+        self,
+        assigned_gpu_ids: list[Any],
+    ) -> tuple[list[Any], dict[int, int]]:
+        """Resolve logical server slots onto this actor's physical GPUs."""
+
+        remapped_groups, gpu_id_map = remap_server_groups_to_assigned_gpus(
+            self.server_payload.get("server_groups", []),
+            assigned_gpu_ids=assigned_gpu_ids,
+        )
+        return resolve_server_groups(remapped_groups), gpu_id_map
+
+
+def _write_json(path: Path, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Write one node-owned metadata file with stable UTF-8 formatting."""
+
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(
+        json.dumps(dict(payload), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
+        + "\n",
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+
+
+__all__ = ["RewardAgentRayNodeWorker"]

+"""Task-bound multimodal reference examples injected into model conversations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import shutil
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Literal, Sequence
+
+from PIL import Image
+
+from .visual import transcode_reference_video
+
+
+ReferenceInputType = Literal["image", "video"]
+_PROGRESS_MARKER_PREFIX = "[[progress:"
+_PROGRESS_MARKER_SUFFIX = "]]"
+_SUPPORTED_INPUT_TYPES = {"image", "video"}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ReferenceInputConfig:
+    """One configured image or video belonging to a reference example."""
+
+    type: ReferenceInputType
+    path: Path
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ReferenceExampleConfig:
+    """One task-bound reference example before run-local materialization."""
+
+    inputs: tuple[ReferenceInputConfig, ...]
+    description: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ProgressMarker:
+    """One normalized progress marker compiled from reference prose."""
+
+    ratio: Decimal
+    progress_points: int
+    start_offset: int
+    end_offset: int
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "ratio": str(self.ratio),
+            "progress_points": int(self.progress_points),
+            "start_offset": int(self.start_offset),
+            "end_offset": int(self.end_offset),
+        }
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class MaterializedReferenceInput:
+    """One run-local image copy or transcoded video shown to the model."""
+
+    type: ReferenceInputType
+    path: Path
+    source_sha256: str
+    output_sha256: str
+    materialization: Literal["copied", "transcoded"]
+    output_frame_count: int | None = None
+    output_fps: int | None = None
+    output_codec: str | None = None
+
+    def media_content(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        if self.type == "video":
+            return {
+                "type": "video_url",
+                "video_url": {"url": self.path.resolve().as_uri()},
+            }
+        return {
+            "type": "image_url",
+            "image_url": {"url": self.path.resolve().as_uri()},
+        }
+
+    def to_manifest_dict(self, *, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        data: dict[str, Any] = {
+            "type": self.type,
+            "run_path": self.path.resolve().relative_to(run_dir.resolve()).as_posix(),
+            "materialization": self.materialization,
+            "source_sha256": self.source_sha256,
+            "output_sha256": self.output_sha256,
+        }
+        if self.output_frame_count is not None:
+            data["output_frame_count"] = int(self.output_frame_count)
+        if self.output_fps is not None:
+            data["output_fps"] = int(self.output_fps)
+        if self.output_codec is not None:
+            data["output_codec"] = self.output_codec
+        return data
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class MaterializedReferenceExample:
+    """One fully resolved reference example ready for conversation bootstrap."""
+
+    index: int
+    inputs: tuple[MaterializedReferenceInput, ...]
+    source_description: str
+    rendered_description: str
+    progress_markers: tuple[ProgressMarker, ...]
+
+    def to_message(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        content: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
+            {
+                "type": "text",
+                "text": f"### Reference Example {self.index}\n\nReference input(s) follow.",
+            }
+        ]
+        content.extend(reference_input.media_content() for reference_input in self.inputs)
+        content.append(
+            {
+                "type": "text",
+                "text": f"Description:\n\n{self.rendered_description}",
+            }
+        )
+        return {"role": "user", "content": content}
+
+    def to_manifest_dict(self, *, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "index": int(self.index),
+            "inputs": [item.to_manifest_dict(run_dir=run_dir) for item in self.inputs],
+            "source_description": self.source_description,
+            "rendered_description": self.rendered_description,
+            "progress_markers": [marker.to_dict() for marker in self.progress_markers],
+        }
+
+
+def parse_reference_examples(
+    raw_examples: Any,
+    *,
+    source_path: Path,
+    field_name: str,
+) -> tuple[ReferenceExampleConfig, ...]:
+    """Parse task-sidecar reference examples and resolve their source paths."""
+
+    if raw_examples is None:
+        return ()
+    if not isinstance(raw_examples, list):
+        raise TypeError(f"{source_path}: {field_name} must be a list.")
+
+    examples: list[ReferenceExampleConfig] = []
+    for example_index, raw_example in enumerate(raw_examples):
+        example_field = f"{field_name}[{example_index}]"
+        if not isinstance(raw_example, dict):
+            raise TypeError(f"{source_path}: {example_field} must be a mapping.")
+        raw_inputs = raw_example.get("inputs")
+        if not isinstance(raw_inputs, list) or not raw_inputs:
+            raise ValueError(f"{source_path}: {example_field}.inputs must be a non-empty list.")
+        raw_description = raw_example.get("description")
+        if not isinstance(raw_description, str) or not raw_description.strip():
+            raise ValueError(f"{source_path}: {example_field}.description must be a non-empty string.")
+
+        inputs: list[ReferenceInputConfig] = []
+        for input_index, raw_input in enumerate(raw_inputs):
+            input_field = f"{example_field}.inputs[{input_index}]"
+            if not isinstance(raw_input, dict):
+                raise TypeError(f"{source_path}: {input_field} must be a mapping.")
+            input_type = str(raw_input.get("type") or "").strip()
+            if input_type not in _SUPPORTED_INPUT_TYPES:
+                supported = ", ".join(sorted(_SUPPORTED_INPUT_TYPES))
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{source_path}: {input_field}.type={input_type!r} is unsupported; "
+                    f"supported types are: {supported}."
+                )
+            raw_media_path = raw_input.get("path")
+            if not isinstance(raw_media_path, str) or not raw_media_path.strip():
+                raise ValueError(f"{source_path}: {input_field}.path must be a non-empty string.")
+            media_path = Path(raw_media_path).expanduser()
+            if not media_path.is_absolute():
+                media_path = source_path.parent / media_path
+            media_path = media_path.resolve()
+            if not media_path.is_file():
+                raise FileNotFoundError(f"{source_path}: {input_field}.path does not exist: {media_path}")
+            inputs.append(
+                ReferenceInputConfig(
+                    type=input_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+                    path=media_path,
+                )
+            )
+
+        examples.append(
+            ReferenceExampleConfig(
+                inputs=tuple(inputs),
+                description=raw_description.strip(),
+            )
+        )
+    return tuple(examples)
+
+
+def materialize_reference_examples(
+    examples: Sequence[ReferenceExampleConfig],
+    *,
+    run_dir: Path,
+    value_max_points: int,
+    video_fps: int,
+    video_codec: str,
+) -> tuple[MaterializedReferenceExample, ...]:
+    """Create immutable run-local assets and a manifest for selected references."""
+
+    run_root = Path(run_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+    output_root = run_root / "assets" / "references"
+    output_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    materialized: list[MaterializedReferenceExample] = []
+
+    for example_index, example in enumerate(examples, start=1):
+        example_dir = output_root / f"reference_{example_index:04d}"
+        example_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        resolved_inputs = tuple(
+            _materialize_reference_input(
+                configured_input,
+                output_dir=example_dir,
+                input_index=input_index,
+                video_fps=video_fps,
+                video_codec=video_codec,
+            )
+            for input_index, configured_input in enumerate(example.inputs, start=1)
+        )
+        rendered_description, markers = render_progress_markers(
+            example.description,
+            value_max_points=value_max_points,
+            field_name=f"reference_examples[{example_index - 1}].description",
+        )
+        materialized.append(
+            MaterializedReferenceExample(
+                index=example_index,
+                inputs=resolved_inputs,
+                source_description=example.description,
+                rendered_description=rendered_description,
+                progress_markers=markers,
+            )
+        )
+
+    manifest = {
+        "value_max_points": int(value_max_points),
+        "examples": [example.to_manifest_dict(run_dir=run_root) for example in materialized],
+    }
+    (run_root / "reference_examples.json").write_text(
+        json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    return tuple(materialized)
+
+
+def render_progress_markers(
+    description: str,
+    *,
+    value_max_points: int,
+    field_name: str,
+) -> tuple[str, tuple[ProgressMarker, ...]]:
+    """Compile all ``[[progress:RATIO]]`` markers into configured point values."""
+
+    max_points = int(value_max_points)
+    if max_points <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("value_max_points must be positive.")
+    source = str(description)
+    rendered_parts: list[str] = []
+    markers: list[ProgressMarker] = []
+    cursor = 0
+
+    while True:
+        start = source.find(_PROGRESS_MARKER_PREFIX, cursor)
+        if start < 0:
+            rendered_parts.append(source[cursor:])
+            break
+        rendered_parts.append(source[cursor:start])
+        value_start = start + len(_PROGRESS_MARKER_PREFIX)
+        end = source.find(_PROGRESS_MARKER_SUFFIX, value_start)
+        if end < 0:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{field_name} has an unterminated progress marker at character {start}."
+            )
+        raw_ratio = source[value_start:end].strip()
+        try:
+            ratio = Decimal(raw_ratio)
+        except InvalidOperation as exc:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{field_name} has an invalid progress ratio {raw_ratio!r} at character {start}."
+            ) from exc
+        if not ratio.is_finite() or ratio < 0 or ratio > 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{field_name} progress ratio must be finite and within [0, 1], got {raw_ratio!r}."
+            )
+        points = int((ratio * Decimal(max_points)).quantize(Decimal("1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
+        rendered_parts.append(f"{points} progress points on the 0-{max_points} scale")
+        marker_end = end + len(_PROGRESS_MARKER_SUFFIX)
+        markers.append(
+            ProgressMarker(
+                ratio=ratio,
+                progress_points=points,
+                start_offset=start,
+                end_offset=marker_end,
+            )
+        )
+        cursor = marker_end
+
+    # Catch malformed marker-like text that was not consumed by the strict scanner.
+    rendered = "".join(rendered_parts)
+    if _PROGRESS_MARKER_PREFIX in rendered:
+        malformed_at = rendered.index(_PROGRESS_MARKER_PREFIX)
+        raise ValueError(f"{field_name} has a malformed progress marker near character {malformed_at}.")
+    return rendered, tuple(markers)
+
+
+def _materialize_reference_input(
+    configured_input: ReferenceInputConfig,
+    *,
+    output_dir: Path,
+    input_index: int,
+    video_fps: int,
+    video_codec: str,
+) -> MaterializedReferenceInput:
+    source = configured_input.path.resolve()
+    source_sha256 = _sha256_file(source)
+    if configured_input.type == "image":
+        _validate_image(source)
+        suffix = source.suffix.lower() or ".png"
+        output = output_dir / f"input_{input_index:04d}{suffix}"
+        shutil.copy2(source, output)
+        return MaterializedReferenceInput(
+            type="image",
+            path=output,
+            source_sha256=source_sha256,
+            output_sha256=_sha256_file(output),
+            materialization="copied",
+        )
+
+    output = output_dir / f"input_{input_index:04d}.mp4"
+    output, frame_count = transcode_reference_video(
+        source_path=source,
+        output_path=output,
+        fps=video_fps,
+        codec=video_codec,
+    )
+    return MaterializedReferenceInput(
+        type="video",
+        path=output,
+        source_sha256=source_sha256,
+        output_sha256=_sha256_file(output),
+        materialization="transcoded",
+        output_frame_count=frame_count,
+        output_fps=int(video_fps),
+        output_codec=str(video_codec),
+    )
+
+
+def _validate_image(path: Path) -> None:
+    try:
+        with Image.open(path) as image:
+            image.verify()
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - preserve the source path in a clear startup error.
+        raise ValueError(f"Reference image cannot be decoded: {path}: {exc}") from exc
+
+
+def _sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as handle:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()

+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class RewardAgentResultEntry:
+    """One completed reward-agent batch result aligned to a LeRobot episode."""
+
+    batch_results_path: Path
+    batch_results_line: int
+    corrected_progress_csv: Path
+    source_traj_id: str
+    episode_index: int
+    num_transition_rows: int
+    progress_output_mode: str
+    progress_value_type: str
+    native_progress_value_type: str
+    native_progress_value_type_source: str
+    progress_value_min_points: int | float
+    progress_value_max_points: int | float
+    progress_normalization_rule: str
+    progress_normalization_scale_points: int | float | None
+    progress_normalization_source: str
+    # Resolve optional audit artifacts without requiring unrelated consumers
+    # to open them. Probability-space evaluation validates the file itself.
+    raw_predictions_json: Path | None = None
+
+    @property
+    def progress_normalized_min(self) -> float:
+        """Return the lower normalized bound implied by this artifact contract."""
+
+        if self.progress_normalization_scale_points is None:
+            return 0.0
+        return float(self.progress_value_min_points) / float(
+            self.progress_normalization_scale_points
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def progress_normalized_max(self) -> float:
+        """Return the upper normalized bound implied by this artifact contract."""
+
+        if self.progress_normalization_scale_points is None:
+            return 1.0
+        return float(self.progress_value_max_points) / float(
+            self.progress_normalization_scale_points
+        )

+def load_lerobot_episode_index(
+    lerobot_root: Path,
+    *,
+    read_is_success: bool = False,
+) -> dict[str, LeRobotEpisodeRecord]:
+    """Index all LeRobot episodes under a leaf or collection root."""
+
+    records: dict[str, LeRobotEpisodeRecord] = {}
+    for dataset_root in resolve_lerobot_roots(lerobot_root):
+        info = _load_json(dataset_root / "meta" / "info.json")
+        episodes = _load_jsonl(dataset_root / "meta" / "episodes.jsonl")
+        if not episodes:
+            total_episodes = int(info.get("total_episodes", 0))
+            episodes = [
+                {"episode_index": episode_index, "length": None}
+                for episode_index in range(total_episodes)
+            ]
+
+        source_subset = _source_subset_for_leaf(dataset_root)
+        subset_slug = _slugify_text(source_subset)
+        for row in episodes:
+            episode_index = int(row["episode_index"])
+            length = _episode_length_from_row(row, default=None)
+            episode_path = _resolve_episode_path(
+                dataset_root=dataset_root,
+                info=info,
+                episode_index=episode_index,
+                require_existing=length is None or read_is_success,
+            )
+            if length is None:
+                length = int(pd.read_parquet(episode_path, columns=["frame_index"]).shape[0])
+            is_success = (
+                read_lerobot_is_success(episode_path, expected_length=int(length))
+                if read_is_success
+                else None
+            )
+            source_traj_id = f"{subset_slug}__episode_{episode_index:06d}"
+            if source_traj_id in records:
+                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate source_traj_id under {lerobot_root}: {source_traj_id}")
+            records[source_traj_id] = LeRobotEpisodeRecord(
+                dataset_root=dataset_root,
+                source_subset=source_subset,
+                source_traj_id=source_traj_id,
+                episode_index=episode_index,
+                length=int(length),
+                episode_path=episode_path,
+                is_success=is_success,
+            )
+
+    if not records:
+        raise ValueError(f"No LeRobot episodes found under {lerobot_root}.")
+    return records
+
